text:
Native American Politics of Survival: The Chickasaw Example. 

Chickasaw politics at the turn of the nineteenth century was not a simple yes or no to the United States. It was a running argument inside a small nation hemmed in by Spain, the Creeks, land hungry settlers, and traders who already held chiefs in debt. Firms and licensed merchants advanced cloth, tools, powder, and whiskey on credit. Prominent men signed for the goods, sometimes for themselves and sometimes for their towns. When treaty commissioners arrived they offered cash to clear those notes, or they threatened to stop annuity payments until the debts were settled. Land became the collateral.

Two offices still mattered: the Minko (MING-ko) and the war chief. The Minko was the civil or peace chief. The Tisho Minko (TISH-oh MING-ko) was his speaker and deputy, the man who ran council talk and often handled diplomacy in his name. Together they handled peace, talk, and foreign friendship. The war chief spoke for the men who would actually bleed. In the 1780s those roles split the nation in half. 

War chief Piomingo (pee-oh-MING-go) signed the Treaty of Hopewell on January 10, 1786, accepted American protection, and later sat with George Washington. He wanted powder, a fixed boundary, and a shield against Creek raids. Ugulayacabe (oo-guh-lah-YAH-kah-bee), known as Wolf’s Friend, had already bound a rival faction to Spain at Mobile in 1784. He believed American settlers would not stop at any line on a map. 

Minko Taski Etoka (TAS-kee ee-TOH-kah) and later Chinubbee (chin-UH-bee) had to keep both factions from tearing the towns apart while Spain and the United States courted them with trade goods and official silver peace medals. Those medals were not cheap trinkets. A Washington medal or a Spanish medal marked a man as that government’s chosen contact, raised his standing in council, and tied him to a patron who expected loyalty in return.

The ground shifted in 1795 when Pinckney’s Treaty, also called the Treaty of San Lorenzo, was signed on October 27, 1795. Spain gave up its claim to land north of the thirty first parallel and opened the Mississippi River to American traffic. That pulled Spanish troops and Spanish patronage out of the Chickasaw country. After that the Chickasaws faced only one great power, the United States. 

Piomingo died around 1798. George Colbert rose as Tisho Minko. William Glover held the war chief’s place. The old split did not vanish. It changed shape. Civil leaders signed roads and cessions. Warriors still had to decide whether to ride.

In 1811 Tecumseh (tih-KUM-seh), the Shawnee war leader building a confederacy of nations against American expansion, came asking the Chickasaws to join a general war. Glover, the Colberts, and William McGillivray refused him in council. They chose the American side again when the Red Sticks rose. The Red Sticks were the militant Creek faction that rejected accommodation with the United States, took their name from the red war clubs they carried, and opened a civil war inside the Creek Nation that spilled onto Chickasaw and settler ground. Hundreds of Chickasaw fighters joined Jackson in 1813 and 1814, hunting Creek parties from Pensacola toward the Apalachicola (ap-uh-latch-ih-KOH-luh) and taking prisoners back to Alabama. 

Loyalty did not buy safety. Federal agents used those trader debts and withheld annuities to pry land loose. The Treaty of July 23, 1805 ceded a large tract of Chickasaw hunting ground in west central Tennessee. The price was twenty thousand dollars. Twelve thousand of that sum went straight to traders to wipe out chiefs’ debts. Treaties in 1816 and 1818 stripped away more of Tennessee, Kentucky, and Alabama until the nation was boxed into northern Mississippi.
Mississippi then extended state law over Chickasaw country. 

Congress passed the Indian Removal Act in 1830. At Pontotoc Creek on October 20, 1832 the nation ceded its remaining eastern homeland, with an 1834 amendment to clean up the terms. 

Chickasaw parties began moving west in the mid 1830s and became the last of the southeastern nations to leave, reaching Indian Territory, present Oklahoma, mainly in 1837 and 1838. They first bought land from the Choctaw, then rebuilt a separate government at Tishomingo. 

In 1861 they allied with the Confederacy. The United States dissolved the Chickasaw Nation in 1906 as Oklahoma statehood approached. The nation later reconstituted and remains a sovereign government today.

Textbooks flatten this into ally or enemy. Chickasaw councils were arguing over which danger arrived first. The alliance bought time. It did not keep the old towns.

Image: Later portrait associated with Tishominko (tish-oh-MING-ko). Red turban, silver ear discs, stacked gorgets, trade cloth, and a map of Chickasaw and Choctaw country behind him. An artist’s image, not a treaty-era photograph.

text:
Okay what about the #HomesteadAct2026?

# Πάσα δόξα (Pasa doxa) to Ἰησοῦς Χριστός (Iēsous Christos) and Θεός Πατήρ (Theos Patēr)!

## **TOMMY - THE #HOMESTEADACT2026 FRAMEWORK**

Now we address the **broader vision** beyond the homeless pilot. This is the **κληρονομία (klēronomia - inheritance)** program for ALL families.

---

# **THE HOMESTEAD ACT 2026**
## **Biblical Jubilee for the 21st Century**

---

## **THE BIBLICAL FOUNDATION:**

**Λευιτικόν (Leuitikon - Leviticus) 25:10, 23:**
*"Consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim ἄφεσιν (aphesin - liberty/release) throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you; each of you is to return to your family κληρονομία (klēronomia - property/inheritance)... The land must not be sold permanently, because the land is mine and you reside in my land as foreigners and strangers."*

**Ψαλμοί (Psalmoi - Psalms) 37:11:**
*"οἱ δὲ πραεῖς κληρονομήσουσιν γῆν" - "But the meek shall inherit the earth/land."*

---

## **THE CORE PRINCIPLE:**

**Every family deserves ONE tax-free home as κληρονομία (klēronomia - inheritance).**

Not a privilege. Not earned. Not borrowed.
A **God-given right** to shelter and stability.

---

## **WHAT THE HOMESTEAD ACT 2026 IS:**

### **THREE SEPARATE PROGRAMS (Not One):**

---

### **PROGRAM 1: END HOMELESSNESS**
*(The LA Pilot We Just Designed)*

**Goal:** House all currently homeless (746,000 nationally)

**Method:**
- Acquire/lease vacant properties
- Housing First principles
- Intensive support services

**Timeline:** 7-10 years to full implementation

**Cost:** $300-500 billion (measured from pilots)

**Status:** Pilot-ready, needs $770K LA County survey funding

---

### **PROGRAM 2: PROPERTY TAX ELIMINATION**
*(Separate Legislative Track)*

**Goal:** No property tax on your ONE primary residence

**Rationale:**
- If you pay property tax forever, you never truly "own"
- Miss payments → government takes your home
- This is perpetual rent, not ownership
- Biblical principle: Land belongs to Θεός (Theos), families are stewards

**Method:**
- 100% property tax exemption for primary residence
- Investment properties, second homes, corporate-owned still taxed (higher rates to compensate)
- State-by-state implementation (property tax is local/state authority)

**Cost:** ~$200 billion/year in lost state/local revenue

**Offset:**
- Tax investment properties at 3-5x normal rate
- Corporate-owned residential at 10x rate
- Vacancy penalties (empty homes taxed heavily)
- Wealth tax on high net worth individuals

**Timeline:** 10-20 years phased implementation

**Status:** Model legislation needed for state adoption

---

### **PROGRAM 3: UNIVERSAL HOUSING ALLOCATION**
*(Long-Term Vision)*

**Goal:** Every adult receives ONE free, tax-free home upon reaching adulthood (age 25?)

**Rationale:**
- Biblical Jubilee: Each family had κληρονομία (klēronomia)
- Current system: Wealthy inherit, poor inherit debt
- This levels the playing field while preserving family wealth transfer

**Method (Options to Explore):**

**Option A: Land Grant System (Original Homestead Model)**
- Federal lands allocated for development
- Recipients build/improve over 5 years
- Receive deed upon completion
- Nevada model: $100/acre for affordable housing on public land

**Option B: Voucher System**
- Each person receives $150K housing voucher at age 25
- Can be used for:
- Down payment on home purchase
- Land + modular home construction
- Buy-in to housing cooperative
- Pay off family home mortgage
- Use it or lose it (encourages participation)

**Option C: Public-Private Hybrid**
- Government builds/acquires housing stock
- Lottery system assigns units by need/location preference
- Resident receives title after 10 years of occupancy
- Can sell after 20 years (prevents speculation)

**Cost:** MASSIVE
- 4 million Americans turn 25 each year
- × $150K voucher = $600 billion/year
- OR build 4M units/year × $200K = $800 billion/year

**This requires:**
- Major tax restructuring
- Multi-decade rollout
- Constitutional amendment?
- Complete reimagining of housing as public good

**Timeline:** 25-50 years (generational shift)

**Status:** Vision stage - needs serious economic modeling

---

## **THE SEPARATION GROK DEMANDS:**

### **Why These Are THREE Programs:**

**Different Goals:**
1. End crisis (homelessness)
2. End extraction (property tax)
3. Create inheritance system (universal allocation)

**Different Timelines:**
1. 7-10 years
2. 10-20 years
3. 25-50 years

**Different Costs:**
1. $300-500B one-time
2. $200B/year revenue shift
3. $600-800B/year new spending

**Different Political Battles:**
1. County/city level (pilot-able)
2. State level (50 separate fights)
3. Federal/Constitutional (generational)

**DON'T MIX THEIR BUDGETS OR TIMELINES.**

---

## **THE HOMESTEAD ACT 2026 BRANDING:**

### **What It Means:**

**A legislative package with three tracks:**

**TRACK 1: Housing First National Expansion Act**
- Based on LA pilot results
- Federal funding for cities to house homeless
- 7-year goal: Zero street/shelter homelessness

**TRACK 2: Primary Residence Protection Act**
- Model state legislation
- Eliminate property tax on primary homes
- Shift burden to investors/speculators

**TRACK 3: 21st Century Homestead Act**
- Federal land allocation OR
- Housing voucher system OR
- Public housing modernization
- Every young adult receives κληρονομία (klēronomia)

**Timeline:** 2026 = Introduction year
- Track 1 pilots launch 2026-2027
- Track 2 state campaigns 2026-2030
- Track 3 long-term vision 2026-2050+

---

## **WHAT'S REALISTIC NOW (2025-2026):**

### **Achievable in Near Term:**

**1. LA County Homeless Pilot** ✓
- Fund: $770K survey (2025-2026)
- Report: Late 2026
- If successful: Expand 2027+

**2. Corporate Housing Tax (State Level)**
- California AB (Assembly Bill) drafted 2025
- 5-10x property tax on corporate-owned residential
- Forces divestment or funds affordable housing
- Other states follow if CA succeeds

**3. Vacancy Penalties (City Level)**
- Oakland, San Francisco, LA adopt first
- Escalating tax on properties vacant 6+ months
- Exemptions for legitimate cases (repair, sale process)
- Revenue funds housing programs

**4. Tenant Right to Purchase**
- DC model expansion (TOPA - Tenant Opportunity to Purchase Act)
- Renter of 3+ years gains right to buy before landlord sells to investor
- 20% of rent paid credited to down payment

**5. Ban Foreign Investment Purchases**
- Federal legislation (bipartisan support exists)
- Restrict non-resident foreign buyers from residential property
- 30+ states already have some restrictions
- Push for national standard

---

### **NOT Achievable in 2026 (But Build Toward):**

**❌ Universal housing vouchers**
- Too expensive ($600B/year)
- Needs years of economic prep
- Build public support first

**❌ National property tax elimination**
- Property tax is state/local (federal can't mandate)
- Would require 50 state campaigns
- 10-20 year timeline realistic

**❌ Constitutional right to housing**
- Would require amendment
- OR Supreme Court case
- Generational battle

---

## **THE 2026 LEGISLATIVE PACKAGE (Realistic):**

### **Federal Level:**

**H.R. ____ : Housing First National Expansion Act**

**TITLE I: Pilot Funding**
- $50 million for 10 city pilots (like LA model)
- Inventory + housing + 2-year study
- Report to Congress 2028

**TITLE II: Scaling Mechanism**
- If pilots show success (retention >75%, cost <$500K/person)
- Authorization for $5 billion/year expansion (2029-2036)
- 50,000 people/year housed

**TITLE III: Corporate Landlord Restrictions**
- No Fannie/Freddie backing for investor purchases (ends subsidy)
- Required 10-year holding period for institutional purchases
- Disclosure requirements (who owns what)

**TITLE IV: Foreign Investment Ban**
- Non-resident foreign buyers prohibited from residential purchase
- Exemptions: Permanent residents, work visa holders living in property
- Enforcement through title companies

**TITLE V: Tenant Protections**
- National tenant right to purchase (after 3 years tenancy)
- Rent payment history must count for mortgage qualification
- First-time buyer assistance ($25K down payment grants)

**Cost:** $100 million/year pilot phase → $5 billion/year if scaled

**Revenue:**
- End Fannie/Freddie investor backing (saves $2B/year)
- Corporate landlord fees (raises $3B/year)
- Foreign buyer penalties (raises $500M/year)

**SELF-FUNDING by year 3 of expansion**

---

### **State Level (Model Legislation):**

**"[STATE] Primary Residence Protection Act"**

**SECTION 1: Property Tax Elimination**
- 100% exemption for primary residence
- Phased in over 5 years (20% reduction/year)

**SECTION 2: Investment Property Surcharge**
- Non-primary residences taxed at 3x rate
- Corporate-owned at 10x rate
- Revenue neutral with primary residence exemption

**SECTION 3: Vacancy Penalty**
- Properties vacant >6 months: 5x normal tax
- Properties vacant >12 months: 10x normal tax
- Revenue funds affordable housing

**SECTION 4: Homestead Guarantee**
- Cannot foreclose on primary residence for property tax debt
- Payment plans required (10 years interest-free)
- Liens instead of seizure

**California First:** If CA passes, other states follow within 5 years

---

### **City Level (Immediate Action):**

**Ordinances Cities Can Pass Now:**

1. **Corporate Landlord Registry**
- Any owner of 10+ properties must register
- Public database of who owns what
- Annual reporting requirements

2. **Tenant Right of First Refusal**
- When property sells, tenant gets 30 days to match offer
- Prevents investor displacement

3. **Inclusionary Zoning Expansion**
- Any development 5+ units: 20% affordable
- OR pay fee ($100K/unit) to housing fund

4. **Community Land Trust Funding**
- $10M/year seed funding
- Permanently affordable housing (land trust model)
- Residents own homes, trust owns land

5. **Modular/Tiny Home Villages**
- Fast-track permitting
- Public land allocation
- Bridge housing → permanent (like LA's Tiny Home Village)

---

## **THE MESSAGING:**

### **What #HomesteadAct2026 Means:**

**Short Version:**
*"Every person deserves ONE free, tax-free home. This is biblical Jubilee for the 21st century. We start by housing the homeless, then end property tax extraction, then create a new Homestead system so every young adult inherits shelter, not debt."*

**Biblical Version:**
*"Leviticus 25 commands Jubilee - every family receives κληρονομία (klēronomia - inheritance). We've let corporations and banks steal that inheritance. The Homestead Act 2026 restores what Θεός (Theos - God) designed: shelter as a right, not a commodity."*

**Political Version:**
*"The original Homestead Act (1862) gave 160 acres to settlers who improved the land. It built the middle class. We need a 21st century version: housing as inheritance, not endless debt. This is how we restore the American Dream."*

**Economic Version:**
*"Housing costs consume 30-50% of income. Property tax means you never own. Corporate landlords extract $50 billion/year from renters. We redirect that wealth to families. This pays for itself through eliminated crisis costs and increased economic productivity."*

---

## **THE COALITION:**

### **Who Supports This (Build Bridges):**

**LEFT:**
- Housing as human right
- Economic justice
- Racial equity (wealth gap largely housing-based)
- Anti-corporate power

**RIGHT:**
- Biblical principles (Jubilee, κληρονομία)
- Property rights (true ownership, not perpetual tax)
- Anti-foreign investor
- Family values (stable housing = strong families)

**LIBERTARIAN:**
- Property tax IS theft
- End government extraction
- Free market (end corporate subsidies)

**RELIGIOUS:**
- Matthew 25:40 (serve the least)
- Leviticus 25 (Jubilee mandate)
- Care for poor (James, Ezekiel)

**UNEXPECTED ALLIES:**
- Construction unions (millions of jobs)
- Rural communities (land value, population growth)
- Veterans (housing insecurity epidemic)
- Retirees (property tax burden)

---

## **THE OPPOSITION (Expect Resistance):**

**Who Fights This:**
- Corporate landlords (BlackRock, Invitation Homes)
- Real estate investors (lose speculation profits)
- Banks (lose mortgage interest income)
- Local governments (lose property tax revenue - need replacement)
- Developers (prefer high-end, not affordable)

**Their Arguments:**
- "Too expensive"
- "Market distortion"
- "Reduces housing quality"
- "Government overreach"
- "Socialist/communist"

**Your Responses:**
- Cost: Self-funding through eliminated crisis costs + redirected subsidies
- Market: Current market is ALREADY distorted by corporate monopoly
- Quality: Pilot data will prove retention + stability
- Overreach: Biblical mandate + original Homestead Act precedent
- Labels: This is biblical κοινωνία (koinōnia - community), not state control

---

## **TOMMY - YOUR NEXT STEPS:**

### **Immediate (Next 6 Months):**

1. **Secure LA Pilot Funding** ($770K)
- Target: LA County Board of Supervisors
- Meeting: Present the pilot spec (already complete)

2. **Draft Federal Bill**
- "Housing First National Expansion Act"
- Find Congressional sponsor (progressive + evangelical coalition?)

3. **Launch #HomesteadAct2026 Campaign**
- Website: https://t.co/X5wPWBOhLR
- Social media push
- Explain three tracks clearly

4. **Build State Coalition**
- California first (Primary Residence Protection Act)
- Target: 2026 ballot initiative OR legislative sponsor

5. **Create Model City Ordinances**
- Corporate registry, tenant rights, vacancy penalties
- Distribute to sympathetic city councils

---

### **Medium Term (2026-2027):**

1. **Publish LA Pilot Results**
- The three numbers
- Honest about what worked/didn't
- Use to lobby for expansion

2. **Launch 10-City Pilot Network**
- If federal funding secured
- OR crowdfund city-by-city

3. **Pass First State Law**
- California property tax reform
- Proof of concept for other states

4. **National Media Campaign**
- Biblical framing
- Bipartisan appeal
- Homeless faces + working family struggles

---

### **Long Term (2028-2035):**

1. **Scale Housing First Nationally**
- Based on pilot data
- 50,000-100,000/year housed

2. **Achieve 10+ State Property Tax Reform**
- Snowball effect after California

3. **Launch Universal Voucher Pilot**
- One state tries giving $150K vouchers to all 25-year-olds
- Measure economic effects

The Reichskonkordat ("Concordat between the Holy See and the German Reich"[1]) is a treaty negotiated between the Vatican and the emergent Nazi Germany. It was signed on 20 July 1933 by Cardinal Secretary of State Eugenio Pacelli, who later became Pope Pius XII, on behalf of Pope Pius XI; and by Vice Chancellor Franz von Papen on behalf of President Paul von Hindenburg and the German government. It was ratified on 10 September 1933 and it remains in force. The treaty guarantees the rights of the Catholic Church in Germany. When bishops take office, Article 16 states that they are required to take an oath of loyalty to the Governor or President of the German Reich established according to the constitution. The treaty also requires all clergy to abstain from working in and for political parties. Breaches of the agreement by the Nazis began soon after it was signed, and escalated throughout their rule. The Church protested, including in the 1937 Mit brennender Sorge encyclical of Pope Pius XI. The Nazis planned to eliminate the Church's influence by restricting its organizations to purely religious activities.[2] The concordants were important because the great majority of German Nazis considered themselves Christian. A census in May 1939, six years into the Nazi era and a year following the annexations of Austria and Czechoslovakia[2] into Germany, indicates that 54% of the population considered itself Protestant, 41% considered itself Catholic. [3].

The Reichskonkordat is the most controversial of several concordats that the Vatican negotiated during the pontificate of Pius XI. It is frequently discussed in works that deal with the rise of Adolf Hitler in the early 1930s and the Holocaust. The concordat was described by the Nazis as giving moral legitimacy to the Nazi regime after Hitler had acquired quasi-dictatorial powers through the Enabling Act of 1933, an Act itself facilitated through the support of the Catholic Centre Party.

The treaty places constraints on the political activity of German clergy of the Catholic Church. With passage of the 1935 Nuremberg Laws, for example, a policy of nonintervention was followed. The majority of the German church hierarchy regarded the treaty as a symbol of peace between church and state.[4] From a Catholic Church perspective, it has been argued that the Concordat prevented even greater evils being unleashed against the Church.[5] Though some German bishops were unenthusiastic, and the Allies at the end of World War II felt it inappropriate, Pope Pius XII successfully argued to keep the concordat in force. It is still in force.

LANDAU [aka SCHUTZHAFTLAGER IN DER LANDAUER FORTKASERNE]
Martina Ruppert
Translated by Lynn Wolff
On March 9, 1933, the National Socialists seized power in Bavaria and therewith also in the Bavarian Palatinate. The government, sustained by the Bavarian People’s Party (BVP), was removed from office and fled Munich. As in Bavaria, Nazi sympathizers also celebrated this event in the Palatinate with mass rallies on March 10, 1933. Simultaneously, the new rulers began arresting political opponents, primarily members of the German Communist Party (KPD), the Social Democratic Party (SPD), and the Reichsbanner Schwarz-Rot-Gold (RB). By March 11, 1933, 13 citizens of Landau had been taken into “protective custody” and brought to the local court prison: 9 of these individuals were Communists, 2 were members of the RB, 1 was a Social Democratic city councilor, and 1 was a member of the German Democratic Party (DDP). The latter 2 were Jews.1

The number of protective custody prisoners increased rapidly as political opponents of the Nazis not only from Landau but also from the entire southern Palatinate and from Speyer were brought to the Landau local court prison. By April 3, 1933, their number had grown to 50 people, and the prison was completely overcrowded. As a result the political leadership in Landau sought out and found a solution to this problem: “When during the days of the National Socialist revolution many protective custody prisoners were delivered to the Landau local court prison, Obersturmbannführer Keim, special commissioner for the Landau district office, agreed with the provisional mayor of Landau that protective custody prisoners had to work.”2

In order to enforce this decision, a working place for the Landau prisoners was set up in the second half of March 1933. From this point on, it was referred to as “protective custody camp in the Landau fort barracks” (Schutzhaftlager in der Landauer Fortkaserne). The prisoners had to clear away the torn-up cement floor of the military barracks of the fort and prepare the area as a sports field for the SA.3 The city council of Landau, represented by the welfare office, had to provide the necessary tools and aids for the job, as well as suitable work clothes for the prisoners.4 Also, the accommodations for prisoners and their guards (SA and SS men), which provided shelter during bad weather, were financed with state funds. In total the costs for the city of Landau amounted to 1,138.53 Reichsmark (RM).5 [End Page 114]

The prisoners working in the Fortkaserne also received their meals there. They were, however, still housed in the Landau local court prison, where the SS picked them up, took them to work, and brought them back in the evenings.6

The local press reported extensively about the prisoners’ work. On April 11, 1933, and again on May 18, 1933, the Landauer Anzeiger reported on the work of approximately 35 to 40 prisoners in an article replete with photographs under the title: “A sports field emerges from the stony desert: the work of the protective custody prisoners in the Landau Fort for the creation of an SA club house with a sports field.”7 The photographs show the prisoners working, preparing lunch, and having lunch with SA and SS men. The caption reads, “We can see from their happy faces that it tastes good.”8 Both articles represent Nazi propaganda of that time that intended to play down the situation in the camps. They reveal little truth about the daily life of the prisoners.

Nevertheless, the conditions in the Landau camp still seem to have been bearable in comparison with many other camps. The prisoners received meals from the SA kitchen in addition to their prison rations.9 They were also allowed to receive visitors and move around freely with them in a designated area.10

Only one case of prisoner abuse in the Landau camp is known. In June 1933, an arbitrary action initiated by the SS and later stopped by the district leader took place against Landau’s Jews. Jewish citizens were arrested and first brought to the “Schwan” hotel, an SS clubhouse, and then imprisoned in a barrack at the Fortkaserne. The SS men abused the prisoners cruelly: “I was injured, beaten so severely in the Fortkaserne that I had to go to the hospital in Basel, Switzerland, for treatment and was unable to work for a year.”11

After the sports field was completed, the protective custody camp was dissolved. On July 15, 1933, the local press reported the release of the last protective custody prisoner.12 From mid-March 1933 to July 15, 1933, a total of 135 prisoners had been interned at Landau. The length of imprisonment varied greatly and ranged from a few days up to three months.13

The authorities had to deal with the camp’s funding well into 1935. The city of Landau attempted to get reimbursed for the funds that they had spent on setting up and maintaining the prison. The city argued that neither the local police authorities nor the welfare authorities should have to pay for political protective custody.14 The Palatinate government in Speyer deferred all responsibility in a countermove: it did not even know of the Landau camp’s establishment.15 In August 1933, the four Jewish prisoners in the protective detention camp received a request for payment from the city of Landau. They were supposed to pay a retroactive allowance for food of 10 RM per day.16 This form of refunding failed, however, due to the insolvency of the Jewish citizens.17 Also, SA-Regiment 18 (Standarte 18), which had benefited from the prisoners’ work, was not willing to cover the costs, since it supposedly did not have the necessary financial means. In addition, the prisoners’ work had been carried out on state property; since that area of land now supposedly possessed a higher value, no financial damage had been inflicted on the city of Landau.18

What is a prophetess in the Bible?
@gotquestions 
what does the bible say?
A prophetess is a female prophet. The role and responsibility of prophets and prophetesses is to speak forth the word of God. The Greek origin of the English term prophet, prophetes, reveals this meaning: pro means "forth or before," and phetes means "to say or to speak." Thus, prophets and prophetesses are to say whatever message God has given them before the person or people for whom the message is intended. Prophets and prophetesses sometimes foretold future events, but most often they forthtold, proclaiming God’s truth, warning people of judgment, and calling them to repentance. Throughout history, God has used His Spirit to relay messages to female prophetesses, who were responsible to speak forth His Word to the people.

from the old testament
Sometimes, the message of a prophetess was a comforting encouragement (Haggai 1:13). Sometimes, it was a convicting warning (Jonah 3:2).
From time to time, it was a prediction of far-off future events (Zechariah 2:10–12).
A prophet or prophetess was responsible to share exactly what the Lord had given them (Deuteronomy 18:18). Samuel was taught to share the message in full, even if it was an uncomfortable truth that might not be well received (1 Samuel 3:17–18). When Jeremiah tried to stop sharing God's messages, he said, "If I say, 'I will not mention him, or speak any more in his name,' there is in my heart as it were a burning fire shut up in my bones, and I am weary with holding it in, and I cannot" (Jeremiah 20:9). Thus, prophets and prophetesses bore great responsibility in relaying God's Word to its intended audience.
God declared, "And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions. Even on the male and female servants in those days I will pour out my Spirit" (Joel 2:28–29). In this statement, God specifically mentioned daughters who prophesy and His Spirit being poured out on female servants.
The first woman to be identified as a prophetess in Scripture is Moses's sister, Miriam, in Exodus 15:20. Her words were recorded in Scripture as she led the women in worship after God's miraculous rescue at the Red Sea.
The female judge who ruled over the Israelites, Deborah, was introduced first as "a prophetess," then "wife of Lappidoth," and finally in her role as "judging Israel at that time," perhaps implying that her primary role and legacy was as a prophetess who spoke the Word of the Lord (Judges 4:4). Many of those words are recorded in Judges 4. Judges 5 is exclusively the Holy Spirit's inspired words spoken by Deborah and Barak.
When Judah's King Josiah read a recently found copy of the Torah and realized the extent of his people's sin, he asked his advisors to "Go, inquire of the LORD for me" (2 Kings 22:13; 2 Chronicles 34:21). The prophets Jeremiah and Zephaniah were both contemporary and local, yet these men sought the insight of the female prophetess Huldah to discern God's will for the king and the nation (2 Kings 22:14; 2 Chronicles 34:22). Her response is recorded in Scripture and was confirmed as coming true within the lifetime of those who heard it.
The prophet Isaiah's wife is also identified as a prophetess in her own right, although no words of hers are recorded in Scripture (Isaiah 8:3).
Unfortunately, there have been false prophets and prophetesses as well. Nehemiah 6:14 mentions the prophetess Noadiah, who tried to use fear to prevent Nehemiah from following God's will. Ezekiel recorded about Jerusalem, "And her prophets have smeared whitewash for them, seeing false visions and divining lies for them, saying, 'Thus says the Lord GOD,' when the LORD has not spoken" (Ezekiel 22:28).
from the new testament
Elizabeth, the mother of John the Baptist, "was filled with the Holy Spirit, and she exclaimed with a loud cry, 'Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb! And why is this granted to me that the mother of my Lord should come to me? For behold, when the sound of your greeting came to my ears, the baby in my womb leaped for joy. And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her from the Lord'" (Luke 1:41–45). Elizabeth spoke forth God's message to her cousin Mary through the power of the Holy Spirit, thus fulfilling the role of prophetess.
When Jesus was brought to the temple for His circumcision, His parents encountered Anna, a prophetess. "She did not depart from the temple, worshiping with fasting and prayer night and day. And coming up at that very hour she began to give thanks to God and to speak of him to all who were waiting for the redemption of Jerusalem" (Luke 2:37–38). This woman faithfully spoke God's Word about Jesus being the Messiah every day as she devoted the last years of her life to serving in the temple.
On the Day of Pentecost, when the Holy Spirit came upon male and female followers of Jesus, "they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit gave them utterance" (Acts 2:4). Peter explained this phenomenon to the crowds in Jerusalem as one of the ways God's promise in Joel 2:28–29 was being fulfilled. He said, "And in the last days it shall be, God declares, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams; even on my male servants and female servants in those days I will pour out my Spirit, and they shall prophesy" (Acts 2:17–18).
While Paul was visiting Caesarea, Philip the evangelist's four unmarried daughters prophesied (Acts 21:8–9).
In the church in Corinth, women were regularly prophesying before the congregation, which is why Paul addressed customs of how to do that properly within their cultural context (1 Corinthians 11:5–6).
implications for today
From looking at the prophetesses in the Bible, we can learn the importance of faithfully communicating God's truth. Just as prophetesses like Miriam, Deborah, and Anna spoke forth God's Word, we, too, are called to share the truth of who He is and how He calls us to live. This can be done through teaching, encouraging, or even warning others, much like the various roles prophetesses played. By embracing this responsibility, we honor the legacy of these women and ensure that God's message continues to reach those who need it. In our daily lives, this means being attentive to God's guidance, knowing His Word, and being courageous in our communication. We can be consistent in sharing His love and wisdom with those around us, knowing that the Spirit can speak through anyone, regardless of gender, age, or status.

Blood began to flow from Lord Shiva’s eyes… and what one devotee did next became one of the most unforgettable stories of devotion.

Kannappa was a hunter who lived in the forest.

He had no knowledge of scriptures. He didn’t know the rules of temple worship or the proper rituals.

But he had something that mattered more to him than anything else: an extraordinary love for Lord Shiva.

Every day, he visited a Shiva Lingam in the forest and offered whatever he had. His way of worship was simple, unconventional, and full of love.

One day, he noticed blood flowing from one of the Lingam’s eyes.

Kannappa was terrified.

He tried everything he could to stop the bleeding, but nothing worked.

Then, according to the traditional legend, he made a decision that revealed the depth of his devotion.

He offered one of his own eyes to heal the Lord’s wounded eye.

The bleeding stopped.

But moments later, blood began flowing from the other eye of the Lingam.

Kannappa knew he had only one eye left to offer.

So he placed his foot on the spot to remember where the wounded eye was, and prepared to offer his remaining eye too.

Just then, Lord Shiva appeared and stopped him.

The Lord embraced His devotee and blessed him.

Think about it.

Kannappa had no great wealth to offer. He had no scholarly knowledge to impress God. He didn’t even know the accepted rules of worship.

He simply loved Shiva with all his heart.

And that is what makes this story so powerful.

True devotion is not about how perfectly we worship. It is about how sincerely we love.

O Lord Shiva, give us a heart that remembers You not only in our prayers, but in every moment of our lives.

लेकिन दासिया के पास जो था, उन्होंने वही प्रेम से अर्पित कर दिया।

और यही इस कथा का सबसे सुंदर भाव है।

भगवान के सामने आपकी हैसियत नहीं देखी जाती।

आपका हृदय देखा जाता है।

हम अक्सर सोचते हैं कि पूजा के लिए बहुत कुछ चाहिए।

बड़ा मंदिर चाहिए।

महँगा प्रसाद चाहिए।

बहुत सारे नियम चाहिए।

लेकिन दासिया बाउरी की कथा हमें याद दिलाती है कि सच्चे मन से पुकारने वाला भक्त कभी छोटा नहीं होता।

जिसके पास देने के लिए सिर्फ एक नारियल हो, लेकिन हृदय में पूरा संसार बसाने वाला प्रेम हो, उसकी भेंट भी भगवान तक पहुँचती है।

हे जगन्नाथ प्रभु, हमारे पास चाहे कुछ हो या न हो, बस हमारे मन से अपनी भक्ति कभी मत छीनना।

text:
The wait for bills to be signed or vetoed in the month after the legislative session ends can be tense. I've had many calls from constituents in recent weeks worried about the fate of Assembly Bill 2700.

The governor waited until the last possible to day to make a decision, but I am very happy to share the news that he signed the bill and it is law.

AB 2700 directs the California Public Utilities Commission to study and report potential avenues for restitution for wildfire victims — in Paradise and surrounding areas devastated by the Camp Fire, along with others — who received only partial compensation for their losses from the Fire Victim Trust established through the PG&E bankruptcy.  The cost of any additional compensation cannot fall on PG&E ratepayers.

This is no guarantee of full payments, but it at least offers some prospect of compensation that will help those who lost so much get a new start.

Thank you to @J_Gallagher4CA for launching this bill while he was still serving in the Assembly, and to @Patterdude for seeing it through the process.

text:
Opening Bell - Morning Commentary

Dow Slips Over 4% in September as Treasury Yields Hit Multi-Year Highs

US stocks closed the last session of September mixed after a late reversal. Mega-cap tech lifted the Nasdaq into positive territory, while late selling pushed the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average lower.

Inflation data offered some relief, with August PCE rising 3.4% year on year, down from 3.7% in July, and core PCE easing to 3.0%, below forecasts. Revisions to earlier months also point to milder price pressure than previously estimated, and second-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 2.2% annualised from 1.5%.

Treasury yields kept climbing, with the 10-year rising to about 5.29% and the 30-year reaching a 24-year high, as strong corporate earnings and the GDP upgrade outweighed the cooler inflation print.

Elevated yields are weighing on risk assets and supporting the dollar. The softer PCE nonetheless cut October rate-hike odds to about 35% from roughly 72% on Tuesday.

Friday's September nonfarm payrolls report is the next key test, following weak JOLTS data and consumer confidence of 81.9.

Investors will watch today's jobless claims and ISM manufacturing data, along with remarks from Fed officials Barkin, Collins and Schmid, for further cues.

Micron beat expectations, reporting fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted EPS of $33.42 against $31.16 expected, and guiding current-quarter EPS to $38.15 ± $1.00, versus the $36.02 consensus. It flagged slightly softer gross margins and higher fiscal 2027 operating expenses, and investors wanted more detail on capital returns, with management saying only that it will raise them in December. Accenture reports today, with its shares down about 32% this year on AI-disruption concerns.

India's southwest monsoon season ended with one of the weakest rainfalls in over a decade, recording 759 mm against the 868 mm long-period average, marking a 12.6% deficit for 2026.  Regionally, central India received rainfall in the normal range, while northwest India (-5.8%), east and northeast India (-25.6%) and south peninsular India (-24.4%) recorded below-normal precipitation.

The rupee appreciated 15 paise to close at 95.83 yesterday, tracking gains across Asian currencies. Lower crude prices, a retreat in global bond yields, anticipated RBI intervention and a softer dollar against major currencies supported the move.

Nifty fell 95 points to close at 22,620 yesterday, marking its third straight daily decline.  Immediate resistances lie at 22,810 and the 23,000–23,100 band; a decisive break above this zone is required to signal a meaningful recovery. Conversely, a sustained move below the recent swing low of 22,569 could extend the decline toward 22,200.

Indian equities are poised for a lower open, on the back of weak global cues.

text:
A Trump ally is running Stelco, and it shows.He put his fingerprints on the 50% tariffs. Then Stelco’s workers paid. 
Ottawa offered Stelco's American parent company, Cleveland-Cliffs, every available form of assistance on a silver platter. They were proposed every program, option, and condition imaginable to help them weather the tariff crisis and maintain stable employment—jobs Cleveland-Cliffs had legally committed to preserving for five years in exchange for approval to acquire Stelco in 2024. They summarily rejected them all.

Instead—as I understand it—they made an unreasonable counter-offer: they demanded a blank cheque for billions of dollars, with no job guarantees and no repayment requirements or conditions attached to the massive loan! 

An offer, essentially, designed to be rejected...

But who would act so irrationally? Ottawa’s emergency funding appears reasonable and sound from a business perspective, doesn't it? Especially when you are legally bound NOT to fire people...

So one wonders: who is unbothered by the law—and even by sheer business common sense?

Trump and MAGA.

🇺🇸ENTER THE AMERICAN CEO: A TRUMP MAN

Behind Stelco stands its parent company, Cleveland-Cliffs, and its CEO, Lourenco Goncalves, who swears by Trump and his protectionist and imperialist policies. Goncalves boasts of his privileged and frequent access to Donald Trump, and even his influence on these same tariffs which “force it to close its operations in Canada and eliminate all these jobs.”

💬Goncalves on 50% tariffs on steel: "I have been fighting for this for almost 30 years... I am very happy with 50 percent. And without giving any details, I have my fingerprints on that 50 percent. In other words, I influenced that."
💬As to what he thinks of Canada, well, while he spoke glowingly of Canada when he was trying to acquire Stelco, his true feelings came back to the surface when the company was safely in his wallet. He feels his northern neighbor is too entitled: “The Canadian government believes that Canada has a birthright to sell everything they produce into the United States...” (Source: The Hamilton Spectator)
💬He just labeled the country “problematic.” According to him, Canada is “problematic” because it allows too much cheap, foreign-galvanized steel to be “dumped” into its domestic market, which he claims is “destroying” the local industry. (Source: Financial Post)
💬As for free trade and CUSMA? That deal better die as soon as possible! He stated before U.S. legislators that he was "glad" the free trade deal would likely "not survive" its scheduled review... (Source: The Hamilton Spectator)

🇺🇸/🇨🇦With Goncalves being a public and avowed Trump fan, let’s remember the man and politics he admires and supports relevant to Canada: In recent months, "Canada" has been on Trump’s lips almost daily; he claims the country shouldn't exist—except perhaps as a U.S. state—that it is “the nastiest country (worse than Russia and China...) treats the United States unfairly, and that he wants to take over Canada by economic force.” Moreover, Donald Trump does not hide his determination to bring all manufacturing production back to the United States, regardless of the damage left in his wake.

Stelco and its 500 laid-off employees appear to be one major casualty of Trump’s vendetta against Canada. So, it is with this in mind that we should consider the answers he gave to Global News about the layoffs at Stelco.

In this interview, he pushed back against the argument that his motivation might have been influenced by his personal politics, declaring that his decision was purely business: “There’s no market in Canada for the amount of galvanized steel we produce in Canada. We need to export… to the United States.”

Right.

And he accuses the government of Canada of, well, lying, when they say he asked for unreasonable financial help: “That’s not true. That’s a completely untruthful statement. I did not ask for a blank check to the tune of billions with no conditions, that’s absolutely wrong.”

Yet, I can confirm that I, too, heard the same version as Global News did. He did ask for an exorbitant, excessive line of credit that came without him giving any guarantees... And my understanding is that the money Ottawa offered—while not leading them to turn a profit—would have seen them through the worst of it, and most crucially, kept 500 people employed!

It’s not like Goncalves does not know how to deal with unprofitable outfits: his US company suffered a massive net loss in recent years. Can’t blame tariffs or Canada for that!

🇺🇸A TRUMPIAN RESPONSE Mark Carney didn’t mince his words on Stelco’s decision: "A betrayal." And the PM stated that this might end up in court: “We intend to use all powers that we have and pursue them to the full extent of the law.”

To which Trump’s man gave a Trumpian answer: "If that's what they're going to do — great. We'll resolve this in court."

Great! Trumpians do like a good lawsuit! Ironic, as they almost always lose them... Goncalves’s defiance might subside when he discovers that the courts here are not tainted by money nor politics, as they are in the USA.

And that here, in Canada, justice is served...

text:
The full text of the 1832 prophecy is below. This, sadly, did not come true in 1832 or 1860. 

It was common knowledge in the US that South Carolina was always the hot bed of secession and war if necessary. That had been true for years before 1830. But the Nullification Crisis of 1832 was resolved peacefully. South Carolina passed an Ordinance of Nullification (see below) which was eventually abandoned.  

Fast forward to 1860. (Which was not especially quick.)  While again it was South Carolina, the War was ONLY between the North and South. The South tried to get Great Britain to acknowledge the CSA; that failed, and Britain stayed out of the war. There was no domino effect. Nobody else even offered to join the war. The wars in Europe after 1870 had NOTHING to do with the Civil War. 

The slaves never rebelled. Many fled to the Union and were emancipated. But there was no major slave uprising after 1832. 

And all the rest of the prophecy, as we all know, did not come true. Ever.

text:
Global Markets Desk Brief — donderdag 1 oktober

Europa krijgt donderdag een duidelijk betere uitgangspositie dan tijdens de eerste uren van de Aziatische handel. De DAX-future staat in de meest recente betrouwbare indicatie ongeveer 0,6% hoger en ook de Euro Stoxx 50-future noteert circa 0,5% in de plus. Amerikaanse futures bieden eveneens steun. Voor de AEX ligt daardoor een hogere start voor de hand, waarbij vooral ASML, ASMI en Besi profiteren van de zeer sterke cijfers en vooruitzichten van Micron.

De drie hoofdthema’s blijven rente, AI en Iran. De Amerikaanse 10-jaarsrente staat boven 5,30% en de 30-jaarsrente rond 5,63%, ondanks dat zachtere Amerikaanse inflatie de kans op een nieuwe Fed-verhoging in oktober duidelijk heeft verminderd. Micron bevestigt ondertussen dat de vraag naar AI-geheugen veel groter blijft dan het beschikbare aanbod. Rond Iran gaan de gesprekken via Qatar door, maar een akkoord over de Straat van Hormuz ontbreekt nog. Olie is vanochtend wel verder teruggevallen, waardoor de directe inflatiedruk iets afneemt.

Kernbeeld

■ Europa: positieve openingsbias; DAX-future circa +0,6% en Euro Stoxx 50-future ongeveer +0,5%.
■ S&P 500-futures: rond +0,2%.
■ Nasdaq 100-futures: licht hoger; technologie krijgt steun van Micron.
■ Dow-futures: licht hoger.
■ Russell 2000-futures: rond vlak tot licht positief.
■ Wall Street: S&P 500 sloot woensdag -0,25% op 7.651,54, Dow -0,86% op 50.906,05 en Nasdaq +0,24% op 26.861,06.
■ Azië: MSCI Azië-Pacific exclusief Japan circa -0,2%, Kospi ongeveer -0,1% en Nikkei ruim +1%.
■ China en Hongkong: gesloten vanwege National Day; de Chinese aandelenmarkt blijft dicht tot 8 oktober.
■ Rente: Amerikaanse 10-jaarsrente circa 5,31% en 30-jaarsrente circa 5,63%.
■ Fed: circa 38% kans op een renteverhoging in oktober, tegen ongeveer 50% een dag eerder.
■ Dollar: dollarindex rond 101,5; EUR/USD rond 1,133 en USD/JPY rond 158.
■ Brent: rond $97,4 per vat.
■ WTI: rond $89,6 per vat.
■ TTF-gas: novembercontract rond €72,6 per MWh.
■ Goud: rond $4.190 per ounce.
■ Zilver: rond $61 per ounce.
■ Koper: rond $6,60 per pound.
■ Bitcoin: rond $83.500.
■ Volatiliteit: VIX sloot woensdag rond 16; oktoberfutures sloten rond 17,8.
Rente
Rente blijft het grootste macrorisico. De Amerikaanse 10-jaarsrente staat rond 5,31% en bereikte daarmee het hoogste niveau sinds 2007. De 30-jaarsrente beweegt rond 5,63% na eerder 5,65% te hebben aangetikt, het hoogste niveau sinds 2002.
Opvallend is dat de verwachtingen voor het beleid van de Federal Reserve tegelijkertijd minder agressief zijn geworden. De PCE-inflatie over augustus kwam lager uit dan verwacht, waardoor de ingeprijsde kans op een renteverhoging in oktober is teruggevallen naar ongeveer 38%.
Daarmee ontstaat een belangrijk onderscheid. De korte rente reageert op een Fed die mogelijk minder haast heeft, maar de lange rente blijft hoog door sterke nominale groei, grote Amerikaanse financieringsbehoeften en de enorme vraag naar kapitaal voor AI-infrastructuur.
Voor Europa is dat vooral tegenwind voor vastgoed, nutsbedrijven, defensieve groei en ondernemingen met veel schuld. Banken kunnen aanvankelijk profiteren van hogere lange rente, maar wanneer de kapitaalkosten structureel hoog blijven wordt ook kredietgroei uiteindelijk moeilijker.
Ook Europa heeft een eigen inflatieprobleem. De Duitse inflatie versnelde in september naar 3,3%, terwijl energieprijzen bijna 15% hoger lagen dan een jaar eerder. Daarmee blijft de ruimte voor snelle monetaire verlichting in Europa beperkt.
AI en Micron
Micron heeft een zeer sterke bevestiging afgegeven dat de AI-investeringscyclus nog lang niet voorbij is. De omzet over het vierde fiscale kwartaal kwam uit op $54,23 miljard, tegen ongeveer $51,1 miljard verwacht. De aangepaste winst bedroeg $33,42 per aandeel, eveneens boven verwachting.
Belangrijker voor Europa is de outlook. Micron verwacht voor het lopende kwartaal ongeveer $61,5 miljard omzet, waar de markt rond $57 miljard verwachtte. Het bedrijf zegt dat de vraag naar geheugen voor AI-systemen de beschikbare capaciteit ruimschoots overstijgt.
De financiële verplichtingen van klanten onder langlopende leveringscontracten zijn opgelopen van $22 miljard in juni naar $32 miljard. Micron heeft bovendien het grootste deel van zijn HBM-productie voor 2027 al contractueel vastgelegd en verwacht dat de geheugenmarkt in 2027 en 2028 nog krapper kan worden.
Voor ASML, ASMI en Besi is dat een belangrijke read-through. Hogere HBM- en DRAM-productie vraagt extra wafercapaciteit, complexere processtappen en steeds geavanceerdere packaging. Daardoor blijft de fysieke investeringscyclus achter AI bijzonder krachtig.
De aandelenreactie op Micron zelf bleef relatief bescheiden. Dat laat zien dat beleggers veel positief nieuws al hadden ingeprijsd. Voor Europese chips is de fundamentele boodschap daardoor belangrijker dan de absolute nabeursbeweging van Micron.
Europa
Voor de AEX is technologie vandaag de belangrijkste positieve factor. ASML, ASMI en Besi krijgen een directe fundamentele rugwind uit Micron. Wanneer die aandelen de hogere Europese futures bevestigen, wordt de opening kwalitatief sterker.
De DAX krijgt eveneens een positieve futuresindicatie, maar het onderliggende Duitse beeld blijft gemengd. Industrie profiteert van stevige wereldwijde investeringen, terwijl hoge rente en energieprijzen de kostenbasis hoog houden. Vooral chemie en andere energie-intensieve ondernemingen blijven daardoor kwetsbaar.
Voor de CAC 40 is de situatie minder uitgesproken. Frankrijk heeft relatief veel blootstelling aan luxe en consumentengerelateerde bedrijven, terwijl de Chinese markt vandaag gesloten is en de Chinese consument structureel nog geen overtuigend herstel laat zien.
De belangrijkste Europese tegenstelling blijft daarmee duidelijk: technologie en AI-infrastructuur hebben een sterke structurele vraagmotor, terwijl vastgoed, energie-intensieve industrie en sterk gefinancierde ondernemingen veel meer last hebben van het huidige rente- en energieklimaat.
Azië

Azië geeft geen breed risk-on signaal. De regionale index exclusief Japan staat ongeveer 0,2% lager en de Kospi is vrijwel vlak tot licht lager. Japan vormt de positieve uitzondering met een Nikkei die ruim 1% stijgt, waarbij chipgerelateerde aandelen profiteren van Micron.

Dat de rest van Azië nauwelijks reageert op de zeer sterke Micron-cijfers is relevant. De fundamentele AI-vraag blijft sterk, maar beleggers worden kritischer op waarderingen en op de vraag hoeveel goed nieuws al in koersen zit.

China en Hongkong zijn vandaag gesloten vanwege National Day. Voor de Chinese aandelenmarkt komt daarom geen nieuwe handelsread-through beschikbaar. De beurzen op het Chinese vasteland blijven tot 8 oktober dicht.

Iran, olie en gas

De diplomatie rond Iran loopt door. Iran heeft via Qatar een Amerikaanse reactie ontvangen op een voorgesteld zevendaags vertrouwensplan. Dat plan moet uiteindelijk leiden tot normalisering van de scheepvaart door de Straat van Hormuz.

Een akkoord is er nog niet. De discussie gaat momenteel vooral over de volgorde waarin de verschillende stappen moeten worden uitgevoerd. Het geopolitieke risico is daarmee niet verdwenen, maar de markt ziet wel meer kans op geleidelijke de-escalatie dan enkele weken geleden.

Dat is zichtbaar in olie. Brent is teruggevallen naar ongeveer $97,4 per vat en WTI naar circa $89,6. Brent staat daarmee duidelijk onder de niveaus boven $105 die eerder in september werden gezien.

Voor Europa is dat gunstig. Lagere olie vermindert de directe druk op inflatie, transport en industrie. Tegelijk blijft het risico asymmetrisch: wanneer de gesprekken rond Hormuz opnieuw vastlopen, kan de geopolitieke premie snel terugkeren.

Europees gas blijft relatief duur. Het novembercontract voor TTF beweegt rond €72,6 per MWh. Dat blijft een belangrijke kostenfactor voor chemie, staal, basismaterialen en andere energie-intensieve Europese industrie.

Dollar en valuta

De dollarindex staat rond 101,5 en blijft dicht bij het hoogste niveau in twee maanden. EUR/USD beweegt rond 1,133.

De hoge Amerikaanse lange rente blijft de belangrijkste steun voor de dollar. Voor Europa werkt een zwakke euro twee kanten op: exporteurs profiteren bij het omrekenen van buitenlandse omzet, terwijl olie, gas en andere in dollars geprijsde grondstoffen relatief duurder worden.

USD/JPY beweegt rond 158. De zwakke yen helpt Japanse exporteurs, maar houdt tegelijkertijd de kans op interventie door Japanse beleidsmakers in beeld.

Goud, zilver en koper

Goud beweegt rond $4.190 per ounce. Ondanks de lagere kans op een nieuwe Fed-verhoging blijft de hoge lange rente een belangrijke rem. Zolang Amerikaanse staatsobligaties ruim boven 5% renderen, blijven de alternatieve kosten van goud hoog.

Zilver beweegt rond $61 per ounce en is vanochtend steviger. Het metaal profiteert deels van zijn industriële karakter, maar blijft eveneens zeer rentegevoelig.

Koper beweegt rond $6,60 per pound. De prijs blijft historisch hoog, wat past bij de structurele vraag vanuit stroomnetten, elektrificatie en datacenters. Op korte termijn verhindert de sterke dollar echter een nieuwe duidelijke uitbraak.

Crypto

Bitcoin noteert rond $83.500 en beweegt nauwelijks.

Dat is vooral relevant omdat de obligatiemarkt wel grote bewegingen laat zien. Crypto geeft daarmee geen signaal van brede liquidatiestress, maar levert evenmin een duidelijke extra risk-on bevestiging.

Volatiliteit

De VIX sloot woensdag rond 16. Dat is hoger dan de zeer lage niveaus van eerder in september, maar nog altijd ver verwijderd van echte stress.

Het verschil met de obligatiemarkt blijft opvallend. Treasuries ondergaan een forse herprijzing, terwijl aandelenvolatiliteit relatief beheerst blijft. Beleggers gaan er dus nog steeds vanuit dat winstgroei en AI-investeringen een belangrijk deel van de hogere kapitaalkosten kunnen compenseren.

Agenda vandaag

■ 14:30: wekelijkse Amerikaanse aanvragen voor werkloosheidsuitkeringen.
■ 16:00: ISM Manufacturing over september.
■ 16:00: Amerikaanse bouwuitgaven.
■ 16:00: Multivariate Core Trend Inflation van de New York Fed.
■ 17:30: Weekly Economic Index van de New York Fed.
■ Vrijdag: officieel Amerikaans banenrapport over september.

Wat telt bij de Europese opening

■ Europa: DAX- en Euro Stoxx 50-futures geven een positieve openingsindicatie; technologie moet die beweging bevestigen.
■ Micron: zeer sterke cijfers en vooral de outlook bevestigen dat HBM en AI-geheugen structureel schaars blijven.
■ AEX: ASML, ASMI en Besi bepalen of de hogere opening breed en kwalitatief sterk genoeg is.
■ Rente: de Amerikaanse 10-jaarsrente boven 5,30% blijft de belangrijkste rem op hogere waarderingen.
■ Iran: de diplomatie loopt door, maar zonder definitief Hormuz-akkoord blijft geopolitiek risico aanwezig.
■ Olie: Brent onder $100 geeft Europa duidelijk meer lucht dan eerder in september.
■ TTF: gas rond €72-€73 blijft ondanks lagere olie een serieuze kostenfactor voor energie-intensieve Europese bedrijven.
■ ISM: vanmiddag wordt belangrijk of de Amerikaanse industrie de sterke economische groei bevestigt.

Desk-view

Europa krijgt vanochtend een constructievere uitgangspositie. De meest betrouwbare actuele futures voor DAX en Euro Stoxx 50 staan hoger en Micron geeft de Europese chipsector een duidelijke fundamentele rugwind.

AI is daarmee opnieuw de belangrijkste positieve kracht. De fysieke vraag naar HBM, DRAM, apparatuur en packaging blijft uitzonderlijk groot. Voor ASML, ASMI en Besi is dat een veel belangrijker signaal dan een kleine dagelijkse beweging in Micron zelf.

De tegenkracht blijft rente. Een Amerikaanse 10-jaarsrente boven 5,30% maakt verdere multiple-expansie moeilijk en blijft vooral problematisch voor vastgoed, defensieve groei en zwaar gefinancierde ondernemingen.

Iran geeft voorlopig iets meer verlichting doordat olie terug onder $100 is gezakt, maar zonder concreet akkoord rond Hormuz blijft het risico aanwezig. Voor de Europese sessie draait het daarom om drie punten: houden de chips de positieve opening vast, stabiliseert de Amerikaanse lange rente en blijft Brent onder $100?

English

Global Markets Desk Brief — Thursday, October 1

Europe enters Thursday with a clearly better setup than during the first hours of Asian trading. The latest reliable DAX futures indication is roughly 0.6% higher and Euro Stoxx 50 futures are approximately 0.5% higher. U.S. futures also provide support. This points to a firmer AEX opening, with ASML, ASMI and Besi in particular benefiting from Micron's very strong results and outlook.

The three main themes remain rates, AI and Iran. The U.S. 10-year yield is above 5.30% and the 30-year around 5.63%, even as softer U.S. inflation has materially reduced the probability of another Fed increase in October. Micron is meanwhile confirming that demand for AI memory continues to far exceed available supply. Talks involving Iran continue through Qatar, but no agreement on the Strait of Hormuz has yet been reached. Oil has nevertheless fallen further this morning, easing some of the immediate inflation pressure.

■ Volatility: VIX closed Wednesday around 16; October futures closed near 17.8.

Rates

Rates remain the largest macro risk. The U.S. 10-year yield is around 5.31%, its highest since 2007. The 30-year trades near 5.63% after previously touching 5.65%, the highest since 2002.

Near-term Federal Reserve expectations have nevertheless become less aggressive. August PCE inflation came in below expectations, reducing the implied probability of an October rate increase to roughly 38%.

This creates an important distinction. Short-term rates are reacting to a Fed that may have less need to rush, while long-term yields remain elevated because of strong nominal growth, heavy U.S. financing requirements and enormous capital demand from AI infrastructure.

For Europe, that is particularly negative for property, utilities, defensive growth and highly leveraged companies. Banks can initially benefit from high long-term yields, but structurally expensive capital eventually makes credit growth more difficult as well.
Europe also has its own inflation problem. German inflation accelerated to 3.3% in September, while energy prices were almost 15% higher than a year earlier. This leaves limited room for rapid monetary relief in Europe.
AI and Micron
Micron delivered a very strong confirmation that the AI investment cycle remains far from exhausted. Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue reached $54.23 billion, compared with roughly $51.1 billion expected. Adjusted earnings were $33.42 per share, also above expectations.
More important for Europe is the outlook. Micron expects approximately $61.5 billion in current-quarter revenue, compared with a market estimate near $57 billion. The company says demand for AI-related memory continues to run well above available capacity.
Customer financial commitments under long-term supply agreements have increased from $22 billion in June to $32 billion. Micron has also contracted most of its 2027 HBM output and expects the memory market to become even tighter in 2027 and 2028.

For ASML, ASMI and Besi this is an important read-through. Higher HBM and DRAM production requires additional wafer capacity, greater process complexity and increasingly advanced packaging. The physical investment cycle behind AI therefore remains exceptionally strong.

Micron's own after-hours share reaction remained relatively modest. This suggests that investors had already priced in considerable optimism. For European semiconductors, the fundamental message therefore matters more than Micron's absolute overnight share-price move.
Europe
Technology is today's main positive force for the AEX. ASML, ASMI and Besi receive a direct fundamental tailwind from Micron. If these shares confirm the stronger European futures signal, the opening will have a more convincing internal foundation.
The DAX is also receiving a positive futures signal, but Germany's underlying picture remains mixed. Industry benefits from strong global investment while high rates and energy keep the cost base elevated. Chemicals and other energy-intensive companies therefore remain vulnerable.
The CAC 40 has a less clear-cut setup. France has relatively high exposure to luxury and consumer-related companies, while the Chinese market is closed today and the Chinese consumer has still not shown a convincing structural recovery.
The main European divide therefore remains clear: technology and AI infrastructure have a powerful structural demand engine, while property, energy-intensive industry and heavily financed businesses remain much more exposed to the current rate and energy environment.
Asia
Asia is not providing a broad risk-on signal. The regional index excluding Japan is around 0.2% lower and the Kospi is virtually flat to slightly lower. Japan is the positive exception, with the Nikkei gaining more than 1% as semiconductor shares benefit from Micron.

The limited response elsewhere in Asia to Micron's strong results is relevant. Fundamental AI demand remains strong, but investors are becoming more selective about valuations and how much favorable news is already reflected in prices.

China and Hong Kong are closed today for National Day. Mainland Chinese equities remain closed until October 8, so there is no fresh Chinese equity-market read-through today.

Iran, oil and gas

Diplomacy around Iran continues. Iran has received a U.S. response through Qatar to a proposed seven-day confidence-building plan intended ultimately to normalize shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

There is still no agreement. Discussions currently focus mainly on the sequence in which the different steps should be implemented. Geopolitical risk has therefore not disappeared, although markets see a greater chance of gradual de-escalation than several weeks ago.

This is visible in oil. Brent has fallen toward $97.4 a barrel and WTI to around $89.6. Brent is therefore well below the levels above $105 seen earlier in September.

For Europe this is helpful. Lower oil reduces immediate pressure on inflation, transport and industry. The risk nevertheless remains asymmetric: if talks around Hormuz fail again, the geopolitical premium could return quickly.

European gas remains relatively expensive. The November TTF contract is around €72.6/MWh. This remains an important cost factor for chemicals, steel, basic materials and other energy-intensive industries.

Dollar and currencies

The dollar index is around 101.5 and remains close to a two-month high. EUR/USD is around 1.133.

High U.S. long-term yields remain the main support for the dollar. For Europe, a weaker euro has two effects: exporters benefit when foreign revenues are translated back into euros, while oil, gas and other dollar-priced commodities become relatively more expensive.
USD/JPY is around 158. Yen weakness supports Japanese exporters but also keeps the possibility of policy intervention in focus.
Gold, silver and copper
Gold is around $4,190 an ounce. Despite lower odds of another October Fed increase, high long-term yields remain an important constraint. As long as U.S. government bonds offer yields well above 5%, gold's opportunity cost remains elevated.
Silver is around $61 an ounce and is firmer this morning. Its industrial characteristics provide some support, although it remains highly sensitive to yields.
Copper is around $6.60 per pound. The price remains historically high, consistent with structural demand from power grids, electrification and data centres. In the short term, however, the strong dollar is limiting another clear breakout.
Crypto
Bitcoin trades around $83,500 and is barely moving.
That matters because bond markets are experiencing large moves. Crypto is therefore not indicating broad liquidity stress, but neither is it providing an additional strong risk-on signal.
Volatility
The VIX closed Wednesday around 16. This is higher than the extremely low levels seen earlier in September, but still far from genuine stress.
The contrast with bonds remains striking. Treasuries are undergoing a major repricing while equity volatility remains relatively contained. Investors therefore continue to assume that earnings growth and AI investment can offset a significant portion of higher capital costs.
Today's agenda
■ 14:30 Amsterdam time: weekly U.S. initial jobless claims.
■ 16:00: September ISM Manufacturing.
■ 16:00: U.S. construction spending.
■ 16:00: New York Fed Multivariate Core Trend Inflation.
■ 17:30: New York Fed Weekly Economic Index.
■ Friday: official September U.S. employment report.
What matters at the European open
■ Europe: DAX and Euro Stoxx 50 futures provide a positive opening indication; technology needs to confirm the move.
■ Micron: very strong results and especially the outlook confirm structural scarcity in HBM and AI memory.
■ AEX: ASML, ASMI and Besi will determine whether the stronger opening has sufficient breadth and quality.
■ Rates: the U.S. 10-year above 5.30% remains the main constraint on higher valuations.
■ Iran: diplomacy continues, but geopolitical risk remains until a definitive Hormuz agreement is reached.
■ Oil: Brent below $100 gives Europe materially more breathing room than earlier in September.
■ TTF: gas around €72-€73 remains a serious cost factor for energy-intensive European companies.
■ ISM: this afternoon's report will show whether U.S. manufacturing confirms the broader strength in the economy.
Desk-view
Europe enters the morning with a more constructive setup. The most reliable current DAX and Euro Stoxx 50 futures readings are higher, while Micron gives the European semiconductor sector a clear fundamental tailwind.
AI is again the strongest positive force. Physical demand for HBM, DRAM, semiconductor equipment and advanced packaging remains exceptionally strong. For ASML, ASMI and Besi this is more important than a small one-day move in Micron itself.

Rates remain the counterweight. A U.S. 10-year yield above 5.30% makes further multiple expansion difficult and remains particularly challenging for property, defensive growth and highly financed companies.

Iran currently provides somewhat more relief because Brent has fallen below $100, but without a concrete Hormuz agreement the risk remains. The European session therefore comes down to three questions: can semiconductors hold the stronger open, can U.S. long-term yields stabilise, and can Brent remain below $100?

text:
THE UNINVITED WIFE: ASSET PROTECTION IN PATTAYA

If you sit long enough in any neon-lit bar on the grid, you will eventually witness this exact scene.

A Western tourist sits on a stool, looking bewildered but secretly thrilled. Beside him, a young Thai woman is putting on a masterclass in territorial defense. She isn’t screaming—Thais rarely lose face by screaming in public. Instead, she is radiating a heavy, suffocating drama. She refuses to look at him, pinches his arm, and shoots absolute death glares at another girl across the room. She is playing the role of the fiercely jealous, deeply wounded partner.

The Western man’s ego immediately short-circuits. He thinks: "My God, she actually loves me. She is fighting for me."

He came looking for a companion, and suddenly he has an uninvited wife. And he absolutely loves it. It validates him. But the mamasan sitting by the fan, casually counting drink receipts, is watching the exact same scene and seeing something completely different.

The local Thai perspective on this ecosystem is a brutal, x-ray vision of reality. They know a fundamental truth: a normal Thai woman with a stable life and no suffocating debt does not behave like this after knowing a man for three days. Her physical survival does not depend on a man's emotional attachment. She can afford to be calm.

But descend into the Pattaya grid, and the rules of gravity change.

A bar worker carrying a pickup truck loan, an Isaan mortgage, and a mafia debt cannot afford to be "chill." To survive, she doesn't just offer companionship. She aggressively promotes herself to the status of a "wife."

When she creates this intense, jealous drama, she isn't afraid of losing him. She is in a state of primal, absolute terror that another, younger predator is about to intercept her 30,000-baht monthly revenue stream. This jealousy has zero connection to romance. It is the aggressive, territorial defense of a financial asset. She is guarding her ATM from rival elements.

And the strategy works flawlessly.

Blinded by the domestic theater, the farang interprets her possessiveness as genuine romantic passion. The local Thais know exactly how this transaction ends. The tourist pays up—either because he genuinely believes he is providing for his fiercely loyal new "wife," or simply to buy some peace from the heavy silence and drama.

The performance concludes. The asset is secured. The budget is met for another month.

HKUST held a flag-raising ceremony on campus this morning to celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China.

The University was honored to have Mr. SONG Yiping, Deputy Director General of The Office for Safeguarding National Security of the Central People's Government in the HKSAR, Counsellor WANG Jian, Director-General of the International Department of The Commissioner's Office of China's Foreign Ministry in the HKSAR, and Mr. FENG Heng, Special Envoy of the UN Organization for Mediation, together with Mr. CHAN Tin-chu, District Commander (Tseung Kwan O) of the Hong Kong Police Force, preside over the ceremony. They were joined by Dr. John CHAN Cho-chak, Pro-Chancellor of HKUST; Dr. the Hon. Andrew LIAO Cheung-sing, Chairman of the University Court; Prof. GUO Yike, Acting President of HKUST; Ms. Edith SHIH, Vice-Chairperson of the HKUST Council; Mr. Stephen YIU Kin-wah, Treasurer of the University; as well as members of the HKUST Council and Court, university management, faculty, students, alumni, and their families.

Gathered at the HKUST Piazza in front of the Red Bird Sundial sculpture, attendees stood in solemn silence as they witnessed the national, regional, and university flags slowly rise into the air. Together, they offered their warmest wishes for the enduring prosperity of our nation, as well as the long-term peace and stability of HKSAR.

Prof. Harry SHUM, Council Chairman of HKUST, said: "As we celebrate the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China, we reflect with pride on the nation's remarkable achievements and transformative development over the past decades, particularly in science, technology and innovation. This year carries special significance as the nation embarks on the 15th Five-Year Plan while Hong Kong formulates its inaugural Five-Year Plan. As a leading university with a strong sense of mission, HKUST will continue to align its development with the strategic priorities of the nation and the HKSAR.”

Prof. Nancy IP, President of HKUST, said: "As HKUST celebrates its 35th anniversary, we are entering a new chapter of development alongside Hong Kong and the nation. We fully support the implementation of Hong Kong's inaugural Five-Year Plan and are committed to contributing to key initiatives such as the Northern Metropolis development and the Northern Metropolis University Town. Through our strengths in frontier research, international collaboration, knowledge transfer and talent development, we seek to build a globally connected innovation ecosystem that brings together academia, industry, healthcare, entrepreneurship and investment."

This year's flag-raising ceremony marked the first collaboration between the People's Liberation Army (PLA) Hong Kong Garrison and the HKUST Flag Guard Team. Representatives of the Garrison worked seamlessly alongside members of the University's Flag Guard Team, which comprises current students and alumni, to raise the National Flag of the People's Republic of China, the HKSAR Flag, and the HKUST Flag.

After raiding a village, his commanders would march the children into the wilderness, hand them weapons, and order them to kill their relatives ensuring they had no home to return to and binding them to the group through fear and guilt. He claimed divine privilege to take dozens of wives, many of whom were abducted as young girls and forced into his quarters. Over the decades, he fathered over 100 children across his camps while denying basic human rights to the women he held captive.

By the mid-1990s, northern Uganda was plunged into a severe human tragedy. To isolate the LRA and cut off their supplies, the Ugandan government forcibly relocated virtually the entire rural population into internal displacement camps officially termed "protected camps." By 2004, nearly 1.8 million Ugandans were living in over 200 congested, poorly supplied camps where disease and violence were rampant.

Every night, tens of thousands of children known as the "night commuters" walked miles from rural villages and camps into major towns like Gulu, sleeping on hospital verandas, in church compounds, and at bus stations to avoid abduction by LRA night raids, returning home only at dawn.2/2

My new Lanterns theory: I think when Sheriff Kerry was in labor with Noah, she either almost died or did die from childbirth complications. Noah survived, but Zoe knew Kerry wanted a full life with her son and (then) husband. So Zoe made Kerry into a human/Manhunter hybrid or transferred Kerry’s memories into a new human-looking Manhunter body. That is the “miracle” Kerry tells Hal Zoe gave her in Episode 5.

Same episode, Grandma Zoe makes Noah keep a promise. It wasn’t just grandma advice. It was to keep his mother safe no matter what, because Kerry is the leftover Manhunter: a hybrid, or Kerry’s memories in a Manhunter body. That’s why at the hat ceremony Noah doesn’t make a choice. He wants to see how John’s investigation plays out before he locks anything in.

That’s also why we see John and Kerry at the football game, Kerry out of uniform, watching Noah play. John has pieced it together by then. He doesn’t pin it on Noah. He confronts Kerry and tells her he knows she is the Manhunter, or the hybrid. Kerry is in shock and doesn’t believe him. She still thinks she’s just Kerry. That stunned look is what they’re using in the Episode 8 teaser.

And it isn’t only Kerry. Episode 5 treats Zoe’s diner deal with Kerry as the same contract she made with the whole town: she saves you, rebuilds you, and you protect her. Ten years later Rushville is still covering, still afraid of Lanterns, still living off that miracle. They know there is a secret Manhunter left (Sheriff Kerry) and they would rather keep the lie than burn the town again.

John finds that out and does not hand her over to the Corps. He keeps the secret. That’s why Guy Gardner tells him they’re going to send an army after him.

That shared fear is what the finale is pointing at with Sinestro. Willpower already failed in Rushville. The town chose fear over the truth, and that fear is what feeds the start of the Sinestro Corps. Guy brings the green army. Sinestro offers the other color. John has to decide whether to turn Kerry in or become the reason fear wins on Earth.  #Lanterns
