text:
❯ Kernel benchmarks: The Review That Stopped at the Cover

A Linux guest told nothing about its chip paid 816 ns a system call; on bare metal, told everything, 144. FreeBSD charged about 50 on both boxes, in a jail, on bare metal, with every switch I could find. Three people asked for the 816 to come down. Between them they had read the headline and the teaser.

On Tuesday the table went up with three columns, one a Linux guest under bhyve, and the essay beneath it said under The Limit that the columns were not a fair race and that the Linux figure needed a bare-metal run before anybody quoted it as a figure for the Linux kernel. The first comment asked me to pull the slide. The second called it fake news. The third was a careful protocol for a different experiment, about microkernels, reconstructed from the first paragraph. One of them came back, opened the text, found a 1997 figure I had hung on the wrong system, and was right; corrected that morning. That is what reading does.

■ DONE THEIR WAY

One AMD Ryzen 5 3600, two drives, FreeBSD 15.0 on one and Debian 13 on the other, nothing tuned on either side.

The critic's own getpid loop, unchanged, a hundred million calls: FreeBSD 49.9 ns, Linux 143.9. The same loop with the syscall instruction from inline assembly, identical machine code on both: 48.9 against 135.1, so compiler and libc are out of it. Linux with mitigations=off, which nobody runs and I ran once to see what the gap is made of: 53.8.

The analyst's protocol, lmbench from one tarball, a second of warm-up, the median of 101 batches, one core: lat_syscall null 51.7 against 160.9, lat_pipe 2.18 against 5.41 µs. SMT off on Linux: 160.7 and 5.45, no change. A second FreeBSD boot: 51.0 to 51.3. mhz read 4198 on both, so the clock is out of it too. Four more measurements, two designed by the people who objected, and the same order every time.

■ THE JAIL THEY SUSPECTED

Tuesday's FreeBSD figure came from inside a jail, and one reader took that as the catch, which is an understandable reading from the Linux side, where a container is an assembly of namespaces, control groups, a daemon and a registry, each with a cost and a project of its own.

A jail arrived in FreeBSD 4.0 in March 2000. There is one kernel, and the jail is a filter it applies to a process tree; the image is a ZFS clone of the base system, the configuration one file of seventeen lines on the measuring machine. getppid never touches the prison. Measured this morning, same binary, same core: 51.0 ns inside the jail and 51.3 on the host, 2.16 against 2.18 µs for the pipe. The heavy answer to isolation is a second kernel per tenant; the jail gives the isolation most workloads need from the kernel already running.

■ THE HYPERVISOR THEY BLAMED

The 816 was blamed on bhyve, in the base system since 10.0 in January 2014. A system call never leaves a bhyve guest; the instruction causes no exit and the hypervisor is never told. The guest spent that time on itself: nobody had passed it the register that says the chip is immune to Meltdown and MDS, so it turned on page table isolation and buffer clearing and paid on every call. The bare-metal run showed the same decision made with full information, Linux still paying ninety nanoseconds for countermeasures FreeBSD on the same chip declines to apply: set hw.ibrs_disable to 0 and hw.ibrs_active stays 0. Both objections assumed the Linux mechanism and ruled on it. Neither asked.

■ AUTHORITY WITHOUT THE OBJECT

A review is a claim about an object; without the object it is a claim about the reviewer.

Mill, 1859: he who knows only his own side of the case knows little of that. In 2016 Columbia and Inria matched 2.8 million shared news links against clicks, and 59 per cent were never clicked at all, the paper's own word for it. Twitter's 2020 nudge to read before retweeting raised article opens by 40 per cent. Kahan showed in 2017, with 1,111 adults and one table shown first as a skin cream trial and then as a gun control measure, that numeracy helps on the cream and polarises on the guns. Nobody contested the FreeBSD column. The objections came for the number that touched an identity, from people who can read a table.

The mechanism is older than the medium. Festinger, 1957: a fact that contradicts a belief hurts, and the cheap exits are to doubt the fact, doubt the person who brought it, or find others who doubt it with you; a thread offers all three. Tajfel, 1971: people favour a side assigned by coin toss, and a kernel is a good deal more than a coin toss. Kahan's group, 2012: the more literate and numerate the subjects, the further apart the camps stood, so the most educated public is the most exposed one, and in my experience the IT bubble is no exception. And Nielsen measured the reading in 2008: a visitor has time for at most 28 per cent of the words on a page, a fifth more usually. Three mechanisms stacked, none of them needing a villain, all of them needing an object that nobody opened.

A counter-proof cost two drives, a boot loader, several reboots and a day. A label cost two words, and the thread pays the two words in reach. The readers and the analysts asked for a method and got a run. The excited asked for the slide.

■ THE LIMIT

The teaser is a claim on its own and travels without the section that qualifies it; I accept that in full, the post carries a hint now, and the process has a rule it lacked on Monday. Triage at the cover is rational, and I drew the cover. The bill Linux pays buys something: on Tuesday VUSec published Branch Target Reuse, which pulls a root hash off a fully patched Intel box in minutes, and a kernel that fears its predictor is not being silly. One thread is one thread, what each critic read is my inference, the crowd found the one real error, the box is AMD where Intel was asked for, and I am the least neutral person in the room.

The slide stays.

Psychology of Child Serial Killer  
Franklin D. McMillion  
School of Law Enforcement Supervision  
Session LIII
Introduction 
Serial murder is one type of homicide which involves the killing of three or more people 
for one month and is characterized by a period of cooling off. The cooling-off period is a time 
whereby the killers do not commit any murder (Knight, 2006, p. 1192). The people who commit 
serial murder are known as serial killers. The crime is not recognized in the United States., as 
there is no current legal code on it. In the history of serial killing, the earliest recorded case of 
serial killers was in 69 CE in the Roman Empire. The serial killer by the name Locusta was 
executed for poisoning individuals from the royal family. In the middle ages, there were serial 
killers recorded in European countries (Vronsky, 2018, p. 15). It has likely been occurring in 
other parts of the world, though it might not be recorded. Research has attempted to suggest 
explanations of the behavior of serial killers and provide an analysis of their personal 
development (Ostrosky & Alfredo, 2017, p. 70). There are two types of serial killers, such as 
child and adult serial killers, in essence (Harmening, 2014, p. 102). A great number of theories 
has been developed to address their actions. Most serial killers have psychological issues, and it

becoming frequent. They are dangerous, just like the adults, as they indicate the same 
psychological behavior (Knight, 2006, p. 1198).

Hedonistic Serial Killers 
These are serial killers, who receive pleasure from killing, and thus the experience of 
murder gives them pleasure. There is a strong link between the violence of the murder and the 
sexual gratification. They can have sex with the victim before or after killing the victim (James 
& Proulx, 2014, p. 595). They plan their crime well, and they dismember the body of the victim 
after the murder. They have an insatiable hunger when they feel that it could be satisfied only by 
killing. An example of a serial killer of this category is Jeffrey Dahmer, who was a serial killer in 
the period between 1978 and 1991 (Ostrosky & Alfredo, 2017, p. 77). 
Power and Control Serial Killers 
These serial killers need to exercise their power and control the victim. They first 
humiliate the victim, torture, and then kill their victim. They do not respect the law of the land, 
and they feel that they are above the law. They also seek sexual gratification. Their main goal is 
to gain power and domination, and thus killing makes them feel powerful and in control. Anyone 
they feel to be threating to them is killed as they assert dominance (Vronsky, 2018, p. 49). 
Visionary Serial Killers 
The serial killers in this category are considered psychotic, as their visions and other dark 
forces compel them to commit murder. Whoever these voices and visions tell them to kill; these 
killers go ahead and kill them. Some of them have undertaken psychiatric tests, which proved 
their being mentally unstable. Some of this type of serial killers are possessed by evil forces, 
which drive them to kill.  
Mission-Oriented Serial Killers 
These are considered as ordinary persons, and they kill a particular group of people. They 
may focus on killing people from a specific religion, social class, or race. Their goal is to 
eliminate the group or exterminate as many of its members as possible. An example of these 
serial killers is Joseph Paul Franklin, who killed young black males, because they had white 
girlfriends (Vronsky, 2018, p. 78).

There are numerous characteristics of serial killers, and these are some of them. First, 
serial killers indicate varying levels of psychopathy, which leads to destructive tendencies. They 
are mostly categorized in the type of visionary serial killers. They see things and forces which 
compel them to kill certain people or group of people. After their action, psychotic serial killers 
are gratified and do not show any remorse. In normal circumstances, they are charming and 
brilliant. Psychiatrists have identified that these people can be dangerous because people will not 
know if they are vulnerable until they become victims of their psychopathic actions. (Ostrosky & 
Alfredo, 2017, p. 73). The second characteristic is that when they were young, most serial killers 
were abused in the family. The abuse might have been emotional, physical, and sexual. This

112). The serial killers were isolated during their childhood and teenage years. This isolation 
involved bullying, and the person is seeking to prove that no one can bully him or her since he or

particular behavior associated with bullying (Carlisle, 2017, p. 17). Some other characteristics

AI Overview
These three names share a deep linguistic and historical connection, primarily originating in Ancient Mesopotamia, the Middle East, and the Caucasus.
Sargon
Origin & Etymology: The name is the Greek and biblical translation of the Akkadian regnal name Šarru-kīn. It combines šarru (Akkadian for "king") and kīnu (meaning "true," "established," or "legitimate").
Historical Significance: It is most famously associated with Sargon of Akkad (24th century BCE), the legendary founder of the Akkadian Empire. Later, the Neo-Assyrian ruler Sargon II (8th century BCE) adopted the throne name to establish the legitimacy of his rule.
Sargis
Origin & Etymology: The name is the Classical Syriac and Armenian form of the Latin name Sergius. It originates from the ancient Roman gens (clan) Sergia, which etymologists suspect may connect to the Latin verb servare ("to guard" or "to preserve").
Sako
Origin & Etymology: Sako operates on a few different historical tracks depending on the region:
In the Middle East: Among Assyrians and Armenians, Sako is a popular, affectionate diminutive (or pet form) of the proper name Sargis.
In the Balkans: In Albania, it functions as a standalone occupational surname for a "church servant" or as a nickname for the Muslim name Isak (Isaac).
In Asia: It is also an unrelated Japanese surname (written as 佐古) meaning "HELP" and "ancient".

From 1997 to 2002 he was rector of the Patriarchal Seminary in Baghdad. He then returned to Mosul and guided the parish of Perpetual HELP for a year.[6][7]

Origin & Etymology: The name is the Greek and biblical translation of the Akkadian regnal name Šarru-kīn. It combines šarru (Akkadian for "king") and kīnu (meaning "true," "established," or "legitimate").
Historical Significance: It is most famously associated with Sargon of Akkad (24th century BCE), the legendary founder of the Akkadian Empire. Later, the Neo-Assyrian ruler Sargon II (8th century BCE) adopted the throne name to establish the legitimacy of his rule.
Sargis
Origin & Etymology: The name is the Classical Syriac and Armenian form of the Latin name Sergius. It originates from the ancient Roman gens (clan) Sergia, which etymologists suspect may connect to the Latin verb servare ("to guard" or "to preserve").

In the Middle East: Among Assyrians and Armenians, Sako is a popular, affectionate diminutive (or pet form) of the proper name Sargis.

text:
🚨 OIL JUMPS AFTER TRUMP THREATENS IRAN — GEOPOLITICAL RISK PREMIUM RETURNS

Oil prices turned sharply higher Thursday as traders reacted to renewed threats from U.S. President Donald Trump against Iran, once again putting the risk of military escalation at the center of the energy market.

Trump said the time had come for Iran either to reach an agreement with Washington or face the possibility of further military action, telling reporters Wednesday: “Maybe you blow them up.” 

The remarks immediately refocused attention on the fragile U.S.-Iran negotiations and the security of energy flows through the Persian Gulf.

But the latest market data require an important clarification: while crude experienced significant intraday volatility, Reuters reported Brent at about $98.67 a barrel, up 0.6%, and WTI at roughly $90.09, up 0.5% on Thursday. So the “almost 3%” headline reflects an earlier move rather than the latest price change. 

DIPLOMACY VS. ESCALATION

The market is currently trading two opposing forces.

Iran has confirmed receiving Washington’s response to Tehran’s ceasefire proposal through mediators, keeping open the possibility of a diplomatic breakthrough.

At the same time, Trump has rejected reports that Washington offered sanctions relief, and negotiations have yet to produce a settlement. 

That leaves traders confronting a binary geopolitical risk:

Deal → Hormuz risk premium falls

Escalation → Gulf supply risk rises

HORMUZ REMAINS THE KEY

The Strait of Hormuz remains the central variable.

Roughly one-fifth of global petroleum supply normally moves through the waterway, making any deterioration in security capable of affecting crude, LNG, tanker rates and refined products simultaneously. 

Yet physical supply conditions have recently improved.

Goldman Sachs estimates Gulf oil exports — including less-transparent flows — have recovered to around 23.3 million barrels per day, broadly matching average 2025 levels. Saudi Arabia has also resumed exports through Yanbu, providing additional supply outside Hormuz. 

U.S. inventories are providing another counterweight. Commercial crude stocks unexpectedly increased by 922,000 barrels last week, easing some immediate supply concerns. 

MARKET PULSE VIEW

Oil is increasingly trading on headlines rather than a simple supply-demand equation.

The bullish side is clear:

U.S.-Iran escalation → Hormuz risk ↑ → Shipping/insurance costs ↑ → Supply risk premium ↑ → Oil ↑

But there is an equally powerful bearish scenario:

U.S.-Iran agreement → Hormuz normalization → Gulf exports ↑ → Freight costs ↓ → Geopolitical premium ↓ → Oil ↓

That explains the extreme intraday sensitivity to every statement from Washington and Tehran.

There is another important pressure building beneath crude: refined fuels. China has suspended most October fuel exports, while Russian supply remains constrained, pushing Asian diesel refining margins to around $76 per barrel. 

So even if crude supply continues recovering, the global diesel and refined-product market remains tight.

For traders, the next decisive catalyst is no longer another verbal threat.

It is whether Washington and Tehran produce an agreement — or return to military escalation.

text:
Washington Irving's "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow," published in The Sketch Book of Geoffrey Crayon, Gent. in 1820, holds a foundational place in American literature as one of the first short stories to achieve lasting international recognition while drawing its materials almost entirely from native sources. At a moment when the young republic still looked to British models for literary legitimacy, Irving demonstrated that a secluded Hudson Valley glen, Dutch-American folkways, and a Revolutionary War ghost could sustain a polished work of fiction. The tale helped establish the short story as a distinct American form, compact enough for magazine circulation yet rich enough to carry atmosphere, character, and irony. Its success abroad, particularly in Britain, suggested that American writers need not imitate European settings or manners to claim a place in the literary world.
The story's importance also lies in the way it fuses comic satire with Gothic suggestion, a combination that later American writers would repeatedly explore.

Ichabod Crane is both a figure of fun-an ambitious outsider undone by appetite and superstition-and a vehicle for Irving's gentle mockery of provincial pretension and credulity. The Headless Horseman, whether supernatural agent or disguised rival, embodies the unsettled memory of the Revolution without requiring heroic rhetoric.
By leaving the outcome deliberately ambiguous, Irving avoided the didactic closures common in earlier moral tales and instead trusted readers to weigh folklore against human motive. That narrative restraint, together with the affectionate rendering of local landscape and custom, offered a model for treating American materials with both humor and seriousness.

Over time the tale became a touchstone for the emerging national literature precisely because it turned a regional legend into shared cultural property. Subsequent writers from Hawthorne to the regional colorists inherited Irving's interest in the past as a living presence within ordinary communities, and his example encouraged the belief that American fiction could grow from native soil rather than imported plots. "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow" thus marks an early moment when American literature defined itself not by rejecting European forms but by filling them with its own places, voices, and unresolved stories.

text:
“We are effectively creating a situation where graduates may feel they have no option but to leave Ireland."

FITZMAURICE DEMANDS ANSWERS AS GALWAY GRADUATE NURSES LEFT IN LIMBO OVER JOBS

Independent Ireland TD Michael Fitzmaurice has written to the Minister for Health demanding urgent answers over the employment of newly qualified nurses in Galway who have completed their training but are now facing uncertainty over whether they will receive contracts.

Deputy Fitzmaurice said it was unacceptable that nurses who had spent four years training and had gone through the HSE recruitment process could now be left without employment because of additional approval and financial controls.

He has been contacted by newly qualified nurses who have outlined serious concerns about the situation in Galway.

“I have been contacted by graduates who have done everything that was asked of them. They completed their training, went through the recruitment process and were led to believe that permanent positions would be available once they qualified.

“Now they are being left in limbo, waiting for positions to be approved and contracts to be issued.

“That is simply not good enough.”

Deputy Fitzmaurice said he understands that approximately 72 graduates were interviewed and placed on a ranked panel, with positions subsequently allocated based on the requirements of Galway University Hospitals and the clinical preferences of individual graduates.

He said approximately 65 graduates were initially offered positions in Galway, but concerns have now emerged over an additional approval process before contracts can be issued.

According to information provided to Deputy Fitzmaurice, only nine positions had received approval as of last week, with five permanent and four temporary positions.

He has written to the Minister for Health seeking clarity on the situation and asking whether HSE financial controls are preventing positions from being approved.

“We are constantly told about the pressures facing our health service and the need to recruit and retain nurses.

“Yet we have newly qualified Irish nurses who want to work in Galway and who have gone through the recruitment process being told that their positions have not been approved.

“It makes absolutely no sense. Especially at at time when reports from the hospital suggest there are already serious staff shortages across the board in Galway"

“The HSE and Government cannot spend years training nurses, tell graduates that permanent opportunities will be available and then leave them without contracts when they qualify.”

Deputy Fitzmaurice said the situation was particularly concerning given the wider difficulties facing nursing recruitment in the West.

The INMO has also raised concerns about graduate nurses and midwives in the HSE West and North-West region being left without employment opportunities, while highlighting vacancies within frontline services.

He also pointed to the recent controversy involving graduate nurses in Cork, where the HSE acknowledged that job offers had been made in error and subsequently withdrawn.

“We cannot have a situation where young nurses qualify, are offered positions and then find themselves being told that the jobs are no longer available or that their contracts cannot be approved.

“We are effectively creating a situation where graduates may feel they have no option but to leave Ireland.

“That is madness when the health service needs nurses.”

Deputy Fitzmaurice has asked the Minister to provide detailed information on:

how many newly qualified nurses in Galway were initially offered positions;

how many accepted those offers;

how many permanent positions were identified;

how many positions have received final approval;

why an additional approval process has been introduced;

whether HSE financial controls or overspending are preventing nursing positions from being approved;

how many graduates remain without contracts;

whether the Government intends to provide permanent positions for these graduates;

how many nurses requiring visas have been employed by the HSE over the past 12 months; and

how many nurses are currently being employed through agency arrangements.

Deputy Fitzmaurice said the Government needed to provide answers quickly.

“It is extremely difficult to explain to a young person that after four years of training they may now have to return to working in a café or pub, seek social welfare support, work below their nursing qualification or consider emigrating because the position they were expecting has not been approved.

“We need to know exactly what is happening in Galway, how many graduates are affected and what the Government and HSE are going to do about it.

“These graduates want to work. They are trained, qualified and ready to provide care to patients.

“The last thing we should be doing is putting barriers in their way.”

text:
Irish firms manage 9,504 leased planes worth $315 billion that is 65% of all leased aircraft worldwide 

GIFT City, India answer to Dublin, has 33 leasing firms with aircraft count still in double digits. India flies about 800 planes today with over 2,000 more on order for coming years. Most of those planes will not be bought outright but rented through leasing companies. 

Right now, most of that rental money goes to firms sitting in Ireland. India wants to change that by building its own leasing center in GIFT City

India passed Aircraft Objects Act in 2025 so leasing companies can take back planes quickly if airlines stop paying, matching what Ireland has offered for years. GIFT City gives lessors 10 years of 0% tax on profits and charges only 3% to 4% on lease payments versus 20% elsewhere. 

Sounds good but timing creates problems. Lessors earn only about 1% profit in early years of owning planes. Returns climb to 40% much later. Current 10 year benefit expires before profits peak. 

Government is looking at extending it to 15 years

IndiGo set up leasing arm inside GIFT City and plans to grow from 78 leased planes to 150 by March 2027. Air India did same and borrowed $215 million to pay for 6 Boeing 777 aircraft. 

Akasa Air plans 60 planes over 5 years through its GIFT City unit. Together, these 3 airlines have about $12 billion in aircraft moving through GIFT City. Government wants 25% of Indian aircraft leasing routed through GIFT City by 2030. 

That still leaves 75% going to Ireland or other countries for now

text:
If I stood among you now, I would not soften the old maxim. If you desire peace, prepare for war. I did not invent the sentence. The Romans knew it before my birth. I proved it with cannon and conscription. A nation that neglects its arms does not purchase quiet. It purchases the hour when a stronger neighbor writes the terms.

Peace is not a mood. It is the interval between contests, and the length of that interval depends on whether others fear the cost of breaking it. I entered Italy with a hungry army and left with treaties because the enemy calculated badly. I lost at the end because coalitions finally matched my numbers and my logistics failed. The lesson is not romance. It is arithmetic. Powder, trained men, ships, fortresses, and the will to use them keep the border quiet longer than speeches do.

In your age the instruments have changed. You speak of missiles that cross oceans and of alliances written on paper. The principle has not changed. A state that cannot defend its coasts, its grain, and its credit will be managed by those who can. Disarmament offered by the strong to the weak is often a prelude, not a gift. I would tell your ministers to count battalions before they count applause.

As for anarchism, I have seen its face. I came out of a revolution that began with rights and ended with the guillotine and empty treasuries. When authority collapses, the street does not become free. It becomes a market for the loudest faction, then for the man with the most reliable muskets. I closed the clubs, restored the codes, and put the prefects back in the departments because France was bleeding from the absence of order. Property, courts, roads, and a single chain of command are not ornaments. They are what let a peasant sow and a merchant ship without hiring his own army.

Those who promise a world without masters promise a world in which every strong man becomes a master of his block, and every weak man pays. I crowned myself because the Republic could not finish its wars or pay its soldiers. Anarchism finishes nothing. It invites the next conqueror, foreign or domestic, who will impose the order you refused to build yourselves.

Prepare, therefore. Keep the arsenal full, the officers competent, and the law clear. Peace is the reward of those who make aggression expensive. Chaos is the tax paid by those who mistake slogans for government.

text: The Central Elections Committee (a political body) voted to bar the Joint List and Ra’am from the October 27 ballot under Basic Law grounds: rejection of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, and support for armed struggle by a terrorist organization. That decision is not final. The Supreme Court reviews it and has repeatedly overturned similar bans. The Attorney General opposed the list bans; broader support existed mainly for barring Balad’s Sami Abu Shehadeh, who described the October 7 massacre as an “important historic event.”Arab citizens of Israel—about 21% of the population—already vote, sit in the Knesset, have joined governing coalitions (Ra’am in 2021–22), and serve on the Supreme Court. The parties Cenk is defending have long records of praising or equivocating about groups whose charter goal is Israel’s elimination.The “5.5 million” are not Israeli citizens. West Bank Palestinians live under the Palestinian Authority in Areas A and B; Gazans lived under Hamas. They are not part of Israel’s electorate any more than Jordanians or Egyptians are. They have repeatedly rejected offers of statehood next to Israel and elected or tolerated leadership that prioritizes Israel’s destruction over building a state. Extending Israeli citizenship to a population that largely rejects the country’s existence would end the Jewish state by demography. That is the actual demand behind the complaint, not equal rights for citizens.A democracy is not required to enfranchise non-citizens in disputed territory who maintain separate governments and armed movements dedicated to its erasure. Treating that distinction as racism is just a way of saying Jews uniquely have no right to a nation-state

text:
I was six months into my role as lead financial auditor for a regional healthcare network when I uncovered a series of shell company invoices totaling nearly $2.4 million. 

Every transaction was signed off by our CFO, a well-respected executive who sat on multiple philanthropic boards in our city.

When I requested the supporting documentation during a routine audit review, he called me into his corner office, closed the blinds, and calmly offered me a newly created "special advisor" promotion with a $60,000 salary bump. 

The catch? I had to sign an updated non-disclosure agreement and sign off on the quarterly ledger without further inquiry.

I knew that accepting meant becoming complicit in federal fraud, but declining meant losing my livelihood and potentially facing blacklisting in my industry. 

That evening, I downloaded encrypted copies of the ledger files onto a secure external drive and scheduled a confidential consultation with a state prosecutor.

Two weeks later, federal agents executed a search warrant at our corporate headquarters. 

Standing in the lobby as he was escorted out was terrifying, but integrity is the one thing no employer can buy unless you choose to sell it.

When standing up for what's right guarantees immediate personal risk, how do you find the courage to take the leap?

text:
🚨 A Sentence That Cannot Be Undone

The failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee is a reminder of what Britain learned at terrible cost: a state that kills will eventually get it wrong, and nothing can put that right.

On Wednesday night in Nashville, the state of Tennessee tried to kill Christa Pike and failed.

Pike, now 50, was sentenced to death for the 1995 torture and murder of Colleen Slemmer, a 19-year-old fellow student on a job training programme in Knoxville. Her guilt has never been in question. Nothing that happened this week lessens what was done to Colleen, or what her family has carried for more than thirty years.

A federal appeals court halted the execution an hour before it was due; the US Supreme Court lifted that stay the same day. Prison officials then administered two doses of pentobarbital. Pike survived both and was taken to hospital.

Tennessee’s governor, Bill Lee, has ordered a third-party review and called off the state’s remaining execution this year. The Department of Correction insists it followed its protocol at every step. Nobody has yet explained why that protocol did not work.

Supporters of capital punishment imagine a system that is swift, certain and clean. Tennessee has just shown the world that the machinery can fail even when guilt is beyond doubt. Britain’s own history shows something worse: the machinery working perfectly on the wrong person.

In November 1949, Beryl Evans and her baby daughter, Geraldine, were killed at their home at 10 Rillington Place in west London. Beryl’s husband, Timothy, was charged with both murders. He was tried only for Geraldine’s, convicted, and hanged at Pentonville on 9 March 1950. The chief witness against him was his downstairs neighbour, John Christie.

Three years later, the remains of six other women were found in and around the house. Christie was hanged for murder, and before he died he confessed to killing Beryl Evans too. In 1966 Timothy Evans received a posthumous royal pardon for Geraldine’s murder. By then he had been dead for sixteen years.

Anyone who wants Britain to bring back the death penalty has to explain how it would avoid another Timothy Evans, or another night like Wednesday in Nashville. They can’t, because every justice system makes mistakes, and ours is no exception.

Execution is irreversible, it has already killed innocent people in Britain, it deters no better than life imprisonment, and restoring it would mean tearing up international commitments Britain chose to make. The case against it rests on evidence, and the evidence is overwhelming.

Evans was no isolated tragedy. Derek Bentley, nineteen years old and with a mental age assessed as far below that, was hanged in 1953 for the murder of PC Sidney Miles. Bentley was already under arrest when his sixteen-year-old accomplice, Christopher Craig, fired the fatal shot. The jury recommended mercy; the Home Secretary refused it. Craig, too young to hang, was released after ten years. Bentley’s conviction was finally quashed in 1998.

Mahmood Hussein Mattan, a Somali seaman, was hanged in Cardiff in 1952. His conviction was quashed in 1998, the first case referred to the Court of Appeal by the new Criminal Cases Review Commission. George Kelly was hanged in Liverpool in 1950; his conviction was quashed in 2003. Each of these men was failed by police, prosecutors and courts who were certain they had the right man.

Ruth Ellis, the last woman hanged in Britain, shows a different danger. Her guilt was never seriously in doubt, but she was executed in 1955 under a law that left no room for the abuse she had suffered. The defence of diminished responsibility did not exist until two years after her death. A mandatory penalty cannot weigh what the law has not yet learned to see.

Nor did the errors stop with abolition. The Birmingham Six were convicted in 1975 of murdering 21 people in the pub bombings. The Guildford Four were convicted the same year. In the aftermath of those attacks, MPs debated bringing back hanging for terrorism. Had they succeeded, ten innocent men could have gone to the gallows. Instead, they lived long enough to be cleared.

Stefan Kiszko spent sixteen years in prison for the 1975 murder of eleven-year-old Lesley Molseed, whose body was found on the moors above Ripponden. He was freed in 1992 when scientific evidence showed he could not have been the killer; another man, Ronald Castree, was convicted in 2007. Kiszko had confessed.

Confessions, eyewitnesses and expert testimony have all sent innocent people to prison, and the Criminal Cases Review Commission has since sent hundreds of cases back to the Court of Appeal, many of them ending in quashed convictions.

The United States offers a live demonstration of what modern forensics can and cannot do. Since 1973, at least 203 people sentenced to death in the US have been exonerated, about one for every eight executions.

A 2014 study in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences put a conservative estimate of 4% on the share of death-sentenced prisoners who are likely innocent. DNA has freed some of them, but it cannot fix false confessions, mistaken identifications, withheld evidence or prosecutorial misconduct. Those are the failures that convict the innocent, and a hanging closes off every chance of discovering them.

The claim that the death penalty deters killers fares no better. In 2012 the US National Research Council reviewed decades of studies and concluded that the research tells us nothing reliable about whether capital punishment raises, lowers or has no effect on homicide rates, and should not be used to make policy.

American states without the death penalty have not suffered higher murder rates than those that keep it, and abolitionist Western Europe has consistently lower murder rates than the United States.

This makes sense once you look at how killings actually happen. In England and Wales, around half of all homicides arise from a quarrel, a revenge attack or a loss of temper, according to the Office for National Statistics. Someone in that moment is not weighing the remote prospect of a trial, an appeal and an execution years away. For the rare, calculated killer, whole life orders already guarantee they never walk free.

Then there is the argument that it would be cheaper to execute a murderer than to house them for decades. The record suggests otherwise.

Christa Pike spent thirty years on death row before Tennessee tried and failed to execute her. In Kansas, the state’s own Judicial Council reported that defending a capital trial cost about four times as much as defending a murder case where the death penalty could have been sought but was not, and that each year on death row cost twice as much as a year in an ordinary prison.

The only way to make execution cheap is to make it quick. Britain once did: Derek Bentley was hanged seven weeks after his conviction, Timothy Evans about eight. Speed is what made their cases impossible to put right.

Britain is also bound in law. Protocol 13 to the European Convention on Human Rights, in force for the UK since 2004, bans the death penalty in all circumstances, including wartime. The UK has also ratified the Second Optional Protocol to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, which contains no withdrawal clause. Reintroduction would mean leaving the ECHR and breaching a UN abolition treaty.

More than two-thirds of the world’s countries have abolished execution in law or practice. The countries that execute most often, among them China, Iran and Saudi Arabia, are hardly models of fair trials.

Public support for hanging tends to rise after a horrific crime, and it is strongest among people who believe the system rarely makes mistakes. The record shows otherwise. Whole life orders already deliver punishment and public protection. What execution adds is the certainty that, sooner or later, the state will kill someone who did nothing wrong.

Timothy Evans was convicted on the word of the man who later confessed to killing his wife. Everyone in that courtroom was sure. They were wrong, and nothing could bring him back.

Pakistan–Powerus Drone Deal: Procurement Opacity, U.S. Capital and the Israeli-Linkage Question - Pakistan has entered into an initial procurement relationship and a broader cooperation framework with Powerus, a U.S. autonomous-systems company incorporated only in October 2025, but neither the Pakistani government nor Powerus has publicly disclosed the systems ordered, quantities, contract value, delivery schedule, end-user architecture or technology-transfer conditions, leaving the actual military significance of the transaction substantially less certain than the political visibility surrounding it. Reuters reported the initial order and memorandum on 16 September, while the contemporaneous Powerus–Aureus regulatory record confirms that Powerus remained a recently formed private company undergoing a proposed public-company combination rather than an established listed prime contractor. Reuters
The transaction does not presently establish Israeli military technology transfer to Pakistan: the verified public record examined for this assessment does not identify Israeli-origin airframes, components, software, intellectual property or subsystems within the Pakistani procurement, and the stronger evidentiary conclusion is therefore that the Israeli dimension concerns identifiable personnel, business networks and related institutional relationships rather than demonstrated Israeli-origin equipment.
Powerus nevertheless sits inside an unusually dense political-financial network for such a young defence company, because the proposed merger with Florida golf-course operator Aureus Greenway Holdings would transfer the autonomous-systems business into a Nasdaq-listed structure, while Powerus financing and the transaction architecture involve American Ventures and Dominari-related actors associated publicly with Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump. The March merger announcement itself identified the Trump brothers as notable investors in the prospective combined company, although this does not establish their participation in, control over or negotiation of Pakistan’s procurement. SEC
The corporate record is clearer than much of the surrounding political commentary: Autonomous Power Corporation was incorporated on 8 October 2025, acquired or combined several autonomous-systems businesses during early 2026, arranged approximately $5.55 million of bridge financing connected to American Ventures, later completed approximately $50 million of private equity financing, and received a separate $20 million bridge loan from Aureus Greenway Holdings as it expanded through acquisitions and technology partnerships. SEC
The September Pakistan engagement therefore has strategic importance less because the available record demonstrates a transformative weapons acquisition than because it places a new U.S. defence-industrial platform at the intersection of Pakistan’s traditionally China-heavy procurement structure, improving Washington–Rawalpindi relations, U.S. commercial capital, autonomous-warfare technology and politically sensitive Israeli-linked networks.
A second security issue arises independently of Israel: Powerus-related technology has been pursued across several jurisdictions while the company describes itself as an integrator of distributed manufacturers, technology partners and research laboratories, meaning that Pakistan’s principal unresolved requirements concern configuration control, source-code access, component provenance, cybersecurity, export licensing, intellectual-property restrictions and safeguards against cross-customer technology exposure, particularly where the same corporate ecosystem maintains relationships elsewhere in South Asia. SEC
The most consequential missing evidence is therefore not a political statement but the procurement documentation itself: without the Pakistani purchase order, technical schedule, export authorization, end-user conditions, bill of materials, technology-transfer provisions and any localisation agreement, assertions that this constitutes either a major strategic realignment or an Israeli penetration of Pakistan’s defence supply chain remain analytically premature.

Pakistan’s Powerus Deal Is a Hedge, Not a Pivot
Pakistan’s September 2026 agreement with Powerus is less a break with Beijing than a test of how far Islamabad can diversify without disturbing the architecture that underpins its military power. The numbers impose discipline on the interpretation: China supplied 80% of Pakistan’s major-arms imports in 2021–25, according to SIPRI, while Pakistan’s total arms imports rose 66% compared with 2016–20. Against that backdrop, the 16 September 2026 Powerus arrangement—an initial procurement plus a wider cooperation memorandum—does not amount to strategic realignment. It does, however, expose the harder question Pakistan now faces: whether access to U.S. autonomous systems, private capital and industrial partnerships can improve technological sovereignty without creating new dependencies, provoking Chinese concern, or importing operational-security risk through a supplier that is already licensing related technology into India.

China still defines the ceiling of Pakistan’s defence choices
Pakistan entered the Powerus relationship from a position of unusually high supplier concentration. SIPRI’s 2021–25 data place Pakistan as the world’s fifth-largest importer of major arms, with 4.2% of global imports, while China accounted for 80% of those deliveries. The comparable Chinese share was 73% in 2016–20, which means dependence deepened before the present U.S. opening rather than receded. By contrast, India’s largest supplier, Russia, accounted for 40% of its imports in 2021–25, leaving New Delhi a much broader procurement base across France, Israel and the United States. SIPRI, Trends in International Arms Transfers 2025

That imbalance matters because defence dependence is cumulative. Pakistan’s Chinese relationship is not a collection of isolated purchases but a system of training, sustainment, spares, software, weapons integration, communications and industrial co-production built over years. Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said in 2026 that Pakistan’s “all-weather” partnership with China was continuing to deepen through CPEC 2.0 and strategic dialogue, even as Islamabad was “simultaneously” reinvigorating ties with Washington. Pakistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Pakistan Governance Forum 2026

The implication is straightforward: Powerus can diversify a capability segment, but it cannot substitute for an ecosystem representing four-fifths of recent Pakistani major-arms imports. The test is therefore not whether Islamabad buys an American drone, but whether U.S.-origin technologies begin entering sustainment, software, mission systems and industrial production at sufficient depth to alter the balance of dependency.

Washington is reopening the relationship through narrower doors
The Powerus deal fits a broader U.S.–Pakistan reopening that was already visible before September. On 29 May 2026, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and the U.S. National Security Advisor in Washington, where the Pakistani account emphasized regional security, economic cooperation and stronger counterterrorism ties. On 4 August 2026, the two countries held their Fourth Counterterrorism Dialogue, covering ISIS-K, al-Qaida, Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan and the Balochistan Liberation Army. Pakistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 29 May 2026 Pakistan–U.S. Counterterrorism Dialogue, 5 August 2026

Pakistan also facilitated U.S.–Iran diplomacy through the 17 June 2026 Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, followed by implementation talks in Bürgenstock on 21 June. That combination—counterterrorism cooperation, diplomatic brokerage and renewed commercial engagement—shows that Islamabad is seeking utility from Washington without abandoning Beijing. Pakistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Bürgenstock talks

The Powerus transaction therefore serves two interests simultaneously. For Pakistan, it tests whether U.S. defence access can be restored on selective terms. For Washington, it offers a commercial route back into a market where Chinese suppliers dominate. That is a narrower proposition than alliance realignment, but it is strategically more plausible.

The India licence turns diversification into a security problem
The most difficult constraint is not political symbolism but supplier overlap. In June 2026, Powerus Defense entered into an agreement granting India’s Paras Defence & Space Technologies an exclusive licence to manufacture and commercialize Guardian interceptor products in India. The agreement predates Pakistan’s September procurement and gives an Indian company rights within the same corporate technology ecosystem now approaching Rawalpindi. Powerus/Aureus Form S-4/A, SEC

This does not mean Pakistan and India will receive identical systems. It does mean that Islamabad must treat software segregation, encryption, telemetry, vulnerability handling and mission-data ownership as contract-level security issues rather than engineering details. A common supplier serving adversarial states is not unusual in defence markets; a common software baseline or shared vulnerability architecture is far more consequential.

If Pakistan buys a Powerus system derived from the Guardian family, the relevant questions become operational: whether Pakistani firmware is isolated from Indian variants, whether cryptographic keys are sovereign, whether vendor telemetry leaves Pakistan, whether vulnerabilities discovered in one customer’s fleet can affect the other, and whether local engineers can audit updates before deployment. None of those safeguards is publicly visible in the current order.

Local production will matter only if Islamabad controls the interfaces
The Pakistani military’s 16 September 2026 account referred to discussions on procurement, production and capacity building, but those categories are not equivalent. Local assembly of imported kits can generate employment while leaving software, sensors, communications and design authority abroad; genuine industrial diversification requires access to integration interfaces, maintenance data, controlled software, manufacturing drawings and supplier-substitution rights. Radio Pakistan, 16 September 2026

The distinction matters because Powerus itself is still scaling rapidly. Autonomous Power Corporation was formed on 8 October 2025, then acquired Tandem Defense for $500, Kaizen Aerospace for approximately $1.8 million, and Agile Autonomy for approximately $3.9 million in early 2026. Its consolidated successor business generated roughly $1.204 million of revenue in the first quarter of 2026, against operating expenses of approximately $6.116 million and a net loss of about $9.684 million. Powerus/Aureus SEC filing

That makes Pakistan valuable to Powerus as a sovereign customer, but it also places the burden on Islamabad to define what localization actually means. If the eventual agreement stops at assembly and maintenance, Pakistan diversifies its vendor list. If it secures software configuration, integration rights and component substitution, it diversifies capability.

U.S. export controls may cap the partnership before politics does
The ceiling on cooperation may ultimately be set in Washington rather than Rawalpindi. U.S. export rules distinguish between complete systems, controlled components, software, technical data and manufacturing assistance. The Bureau of Industry and Security amended drone-export controls in 2026, but the regulatory treatment still depends on platform capability, end use, destination and technology classification. U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security, Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports

For Pakistan, this creates an asymmetry between purchasing and sovereignty. Buying a finished interceptor is one regulatory problem; receiving source code, secure communications architecture, manufacturing drawings or advanced autonomy software is another. The deeper the transfer, the greater Washington’s concern over technology exposure inside a force structure where Chinese-origin platforms are pervasive.

That friction is structural. Pakistan wants local production and reduced dependency; U.S. regulators want end-use control and protection of sensitive technology. A Powerus programme that cannot move beyond finished products would still have political value, but it would do little to change the technological dependency that Islamabad says it wants to reduce.

The Israel contradiction is political, not yet technological
Pakistan’s formal position on Israel remained unchanged after the Powerus agreement. In its 4 June 2026 briefing, the Foreign Ministry said Pakistan’s position on the Abraham Accords had not changed, and on 26 September 2026 Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar again backed a Palestinian state on the pre-June 1967 borders with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital. Pakistani passports also remain formally invalid for travel to Israel. Pakistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 4 June 2026 Pakistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, 26 September 2026

The Powerus relationship nevertheless places Islamabad inside a politically sensitive network. Ziv Marom, a Powerus technical leader, states that he began his career in the Israel Defense Forces Intelligence Corps; Michael Sinensky, a Powerus director expected to hold roughly 19% of post-merger voting power, is also president of the Worldwide Friends Foundation, whose Israel Friends mission publicly describes support to Israeli defence and security users with drones, surveillance systems and related technology. Ziv Marom biography Israel Friends, Advanced Technology Powerus/Aureus Prospectus, SEC

That is enough to create political exposure, but not enough to establish Israeli participation in Pakistan’s procurement. No bill of materials, export licence or supplier record in the dossier demonstrates Israeli-origin hardware or software entering the Pakistani order. The distinction matters because a U.S. company with Israeli-linked personnel is not the same legal or strategic category as an Israeli defence export.

The next 12–24 months will show whether Pakistan bought optionality or dependency
The decisive indicators between late 2026 and 2028 will be measurable: follow-on Powerus orders; a Pakistani manufacturing entity; U.S. licences covering technical data rather than only finished systems; customer-specific software separation from the Indian programme; and any sustained reduction in China’s share of Pakistani arms imports. Without those changes, Powerus remains a niche diversification channel inside a China-dominant force structure.

The cost of inaction would fall first on Pakistan’s military planners and domestic industry. If Islamabad buys U.S. hardware without securing data sovereignty, integration rights and software separation, it risks replacing one concentrated dependency with several smaller ones while adding support and interoperability costs. If Washington restricts transfer depth, Pakistani industry gains assembly but little design authority. If Powerus cannot compartmentalize India and Pakistan technically, operational-security risk rises precisely in the counter-UAS domain that both states are expanding.

The political cost would fall on Islamabad. Pakistan can sustain simultaneous relationships with Beijing and Washington, and it can preserve non-recognition of Israel while contracting with a U.S. company whose personnel have Israeli links. What it cannot sustain indefinitely is strategic ambiguity without contractual precision. Over the next 12–24 months, the procurement documents—not the diplomatic language—will determine whether Powerus becomes evidence of genuine diversification or merely another foreign dependency added to the balance sheet.

Weat-Point  Lesson  Plan  Oct..  2,  2926-‘Terrorism  On  Board!  A  Case Study of Fly Dubai Flight FZ1073

Gentlemen:

Reconvene for 8-minute brief-backs.  
Assessment / Close
Exit  ticket (written, 3–4 sentences): 

”The single most important lesson this incident offers West Point cadets about insider threats in high-value transportation instances.”

Notes for Instructor:
a.  Keep discussion at the level of facts, official characterizations, and second-order effects. 
B. Do not reconstruct or speculate on specific techniques used in the cockpit. 
C.  Emphasize that the formal investigation by UAE, Saudi, and other authorities is ongoing and motives are not yet established. 
D.  Use the case to reinforce disciplined sourcing and the difference between political statements and completed investigations.

Audience: Cadets (current events / national security / aviation & insider-threat module)

Duration: (50–75 minutes )

Learning Objectives:
By the end of the session cadets will be able to:Summarize the verified sequence of events and official statements from 30 September 2026.

Distinguish confirmed facts from early official characterizations and ongoing investigations.

Analyze the incident as a potential insider-threat / unlawful-interference case and its implications for civil aviation security and regional cooperation (UAE–Israel–Saudi Arabia).

Identify lessons for command, passenger/crew response, and multinational coordination.
Hook / Opening (5 min)

Show the flight-path anomaly (sharp descent of more than 14,000 ft in under 30 seconds, squawk 7700 then 7500) and Netanyahu’s public statement that a crew member stabbed the other pilot and appeared to be attempting to crash the aircraft carrying mostly Israeli passengers. 

Ask: “What changes when the threat is already inside the flight deck?”.com.

Core  Facts (verified as of 30 Sep 2026 evening)Flydubai FZ1073 (Boeing 737) departed Dubai International for Tel Aviv.

An altercation occurred in the flight deck. Israeli officials stated the co-pilot (identified in reporting as Omani) stabbed the captain and attempted to sabotage the aircraft. 

The plane transmitted emergency codes and made an erratic descent before diverting.  https://t.co/N0Du4NOlHu

Passengers and on-duty flydubai crew traveling as passengers forced entry, subdued the attacker, and helped stabilize the Aurcraft.

 It landed safely at Tabuk, Saudi Arabia. 

Both pilots were injured and hospitalized; no passengers were reported seriously hurt.  com
Saudi authorities arrested the suspect. 

Passengers were later flown onward to Israel on a replacement aircraft.

Flydubai and the UAE GCAA described it as a “security incident” / “altercation,” confirmed the aircraft was secured by crew on board, and urged against speculation pending investigation. 

Israeli leaders (Netanyahu, Defense Minister Katz) characterized it as an attempted terror attack. Motives remain officially unconfirmed. https://t.co/jFNvgMvZ3w

Discussion Questions:
How does an insider threat on the flight deck differ from a classic external hijacking in terms of detection time, response options, and required protocols?

What role did passenger intervention play, and what are the command-and-control implications when civilians must act inside a cockpit?

The flight operated under post-Abraham Accords UAE–Israel routes and diverted to Saudi Arabia. 

What does the multinational response (UAE investigation, Saudi arrest and medical care, Israeli scramble and later escort) reveal about current security cooperation and remaining frictions?

How should investigators weigh mental-health versus ideological explanations at this early stage? What evidence would be needed to classify it as terrorism?

Activity (20–25 min)
Divide into three groups:

Group A: 
Reconstruct the timeline using only official airline/GCAA and Israeli government statements. Flag discrepancies.

Group B: 
Map stakeholders and legal jurisdictions (UAE operator, Saudi landing site, Israeli destination and passengers, possible nationality of the suspect).

Group C: 
Draft three immediate policy or training recommendations for civil aviation and military liaison officers (cockpit access, dead-man / two-person rules, passenger briefing, information-sharing).

Regards,

text:
Margaret Tudor reached her brother's border heavily pregnant and was told to wait. The queen of Scotland could not step into England until Henry VIII said she could... 

She entered England on 30 September 1515, accompanied by her new husband and a small household. Her two sons were not with her. James V, King of Scots, not yet four years old, and his younger brother Alexander, Duke of Ross, were in the care of the man who had taken her regency.

Three years earlier, none of this would have seemed possible. Margaret had been Queen of Scotland, wife to James IV, and after his death at Flodden in September 1513 she became regent for their infant son. She held real power in her own right, named in James IV's will as regent for as long as she remained a widow. That final clause would prove to be the trap that destroyed her.

On 6 August 1514, Margaret married again, in secret, in the parish church of Kinnoull near Perth. Her new husband was Archibald Douglas, 6th Earl of Angus, head of one of Scotland's most powerful noble families. Whatever affection or calculation lay behind the match, its political consequence was immediate and severe: under the terms of James IV's will, Margaret's remarriage ended her regency outright. She had married for herself and lost the regency in the same act.

Into the vacancy stepped John Stewart, Duke of Albany, a cousin of the dead king summoned from France by the Scottish council to take up the regency Margaret could no longer hold. Albany's authority depended on controlling the person of the young king. He had no intention of leaving James V, or his brother, in the household of a mother who had just allied herself by marriage to the Douglas faction.

Margaret resisted. For months she held her sons at Stirling Castle, resisting Albany's demands and appealing to her brother, Henry VIII, for support. Henry had been urging her for some time to bring the boys south into England, where he could offer them protection and, not incidentally, considerable leverage over Scottish affairs. Margaret refused for as long as she believed there was a way to keep her sons in Scotland under her own protection.

There was not. In August 1515, with Albany's forces surrounding Stirling and her position untenable, Margaret surrendered custody of both boys. James V and Alexander passed into the regent's hands. Margaret, married to a man whose own political standing was now under threat, and pregnant with his child, no longer had a regency or her sons.

She fled south with Angus.

She had gone to Linlithgow Palace for her lying-in, and from there she rode for Tantallon, the Douglas fortress on the coast, leaving a coffer of jewels behind in the keeping of a Scottish knight, Alexander Jardine of Applegarth. She went on toward the border, to Blackadder Castle. Albany's letters followed her to both.

At Blackadder she could go no further. She was Henry VIII's sister, but she could not cross into his kingdom without his leave, and she waited for it, heavily pregnant, on the edge of another country. It came on 30 September.

The journey was not a clean escape into safety. Margaret crossed the border, but the strain of travel while heavily pregnant, combined with her own poor health, forced the party to stop before they could reach the greater security of Morpeth. They took refuge instead at Harbottle Castle, a remote border fortress in Northumberland held by Thomas, 2nd Lord Dacre. It was there, within a week of her crossing, that Margaret went into labour.

There was no royal ceremony, no gathering of Scottish nobles, none of the state that had attended the birth of James V three years before. Margaret gave birth at Harbottle to a daughter, whom she named Margaret after herself.

text:
My fellow Nigerians, please read this to the end.

Today, as Nigeria marks 66 years of independence, I cannot begin with celebration, when so many homes begin their mornings with calculations of survival? Somewhere, a mother is staring into a pot and calculating what the family can afford to eat. 
Somewhere, a father has received his salary but knows that food, transportation, electricity, rent and school fees have already swallowed it. Somewhere, a farmer is afraid of the road to his own farmland. Somewhere, a graduate is carrying another file of unanswered applications. Before we fly the green-and-white flag, let us ask a harder question: what does independence mean when millions still struggle for the elementary dignity of survival?

They told us removing fuel subsidy would save the country and build infrastructure. Instead, petrol prices multiplied, transportation costs climbed and the shock travelled through almost every part of the economy. The World Bank itself concluded that subsidy removal tripled retail petrol prices in 2023, followed by another increase of roughly 50% through early October 2024, while acknowledging the intense pressure these reforms placed on households and businesses.

 What exactly are we celebrating when basic survival has become a daily struggle for millions? Reform cannot be measured only by what government saves. It must also be measured by what citizens receive for their sacrifice.

Then look at the naira. In May 2023, the official exchange rate was around ₦460 to the dollar. Exchange-rate unification was intended to eliminate distortions, but the subsequent depreciation also produced substantial knock-on effects on prices, something the World Bank itself acknowledges. Currency depreciation is not merely a number crawling across a television screen. It enters the pharmacy through imported medicine. It enters the factory through machinery and raw materials. It enters the spare-parts market. It enters school fees. Eventually it enters the Nigerian kitchen. Our mothers carry more naira into the market and return with fewer goods. That is what depreciation looks like when statistics acquire human faces.

Speech without action cannot fill a hungry stomach. We are tired of hearing promises of "Renewed Hope" while hunger remains widespread across the land. The World Bank estimates that 69.6% of Nigerians lived below the lower-middle-income poverty line in 2025, while 50.8%, about 123 million human beings, lived in extreme poverty. Think about that number. One hundred and twenty-three million Nigerians. These are not decimal points. They are mothers, fathers and children. How do you tell a family struggling to afford food to raise a flag and pretend that independence has reached their dining table?

Consider electricity. Band A tariffs were sharply increased in 2024, with NERC's records showing tariffs around ₦200 per kWh for some Band A categories later that year. NERC itself says Band A customers are supposed to receive a minimum of 20 hours of electricity daily. So the Nigerian welder, tailor, barber and small manufacturer paying those tariffs has every right to demand the corresponding service. When a business pays an electricity bill and then buys fuel to generate its own electricity, something is profoundly wrong with the economics of production. Independence should mean increasing our capacity to produce, not teaching entrepreneurs how to survive unreliable infrastructure.

Every October 1, government speaks about economic recovery, yet Nigeria carries substantial domestic and external debt. Debt itself is not evil. Serious countries borrow to finance productive infrastructure. The question is what tomorrow's Nigerians inherit alongside today's liabilities. If our children inherit railways, reliable electricity, industries, schools and hospitals, they inherit assets alongside the debt. But if they inherit obligations without productive assets capable of paying for them, then future generations have been handed a bill they were never present to approve.

The administration continuously asks citizens to endure temporary pain and make sacrifices for the country. But Nigerians are entitled to ask whether sacrifice is being visibly shared. A mother reducing meals understands sacrifice. A civil servant walking part of the journey to work understands sacrifice. A businessman watching operating costs consume his capital understands sacrifice. Leadership requires leading by example. Austerity loses moral authority whenever ordinary people believe those imposing it are protected from its consequences.

How do we celebrate more than six decades of independence when farmers in parts of the North cannot safely cultivate their own land? Food security becomes impossible when agricultural communities live under banditry, kidnapping and insurgency. A farmer driven from his land is not merely another security statistic. He is tomorrow's reduction in food production. He is tomorrow's higher market price. He is tomorrow's hungry household. When those who feed the country are afraid, eventually the whole country eats the consequences.

Our brightest doctors, engineers, nurses, researchers and technology workers continue to seek opportunities abroad. Migration itself is not a national tragedy. Nigerians have travelled and prospered across the world for generations. The tragedy begins when leaving becomes less an adventure than an escape from limited opportunity. A nation that educates talented young people but cannot create enough productive opportunities for them risks transferring the return on its educational investment to other economies.

Our public universities continue to confront serious pressures around funding, infrastructure, staffing and affordability. An inadequately educated population cannot sustain an independent economy, no matter how inspiring an Independence Day speech sounds. The child of a poor Nigerian may possess the mind of a world-class scientist, surgeon or engineer. But intelligence does not pay fees, repair laboratories or provide research funding. Every brilliant child denied opportunity is productive capacity Nigeria voluntarily throws away.

True independence relies on strong, trustworthy democratic institutions. When citizens lose confidence in electoral processes or judicial institutions, democracy becomes weaker. Elections must not merely be conducted. Citizens must believe that lawful votes count, institutions act impartially and political disagreements can be resolved peacefully. Self-government means little if citizens stop trusting the mechanisms through which they choose those who govern them.

Our subnational governments must also answer questions. Higher FAAC transfers have strengthened state revenues and capital spending, but the World Bank says outcomes remain uneven and dependence on federal transfers has increased. State leaders cannot simply blame Abuja while Abuja tells Nigerians to wait for benefits to trickle down. Nigerians should ask every governor and local government chairman: what did you receive, what did you spend, and what changed in my community? Accountability must travel from the Presidential Villa to every Government House and local-government headquarters.

We were promised that painful reforms would yield macroeconomic stability. Here, we must tell the whole truth. Inflation has fallen substantially from its earlier peak, the external position has strengthened and reserves have improved. Those are real gains. But the same World Bank says 123 million Nigerians lived in extreme poverty in 2025, while its projections still place poverty at extraordinarily high levels. So the question is not whether macroeconomic indicators matter. They do. The question is when macroeconomic recovery becomes household recovery. You cannot feed children with a current-account surplus. Recovery must eventually arrive at the kitchen table.

The British left in 1960, but independence was never meant merely to replace foreign colonial masters with domestic political elites. The public treasury belongs to Nigerians. Every naira wasted has an opportunity cost. It may be a classroom not repaired, medicine not purchased, a road left unfinished or a security post left without adequate resources. Changing who controls government without strengthening accountability does not complete the work of independence.

Government is expanding revenue collection and reforming taxation while Nigerians have also absorbed higher tariffs and subsidy reforms. But where is the corresponding social protection and improvement in public services? Too many citizens provide significant portions of their own security, water, electricity, education and healthcare. Government has a legitimate right to collect taxes, but taxation creates obligations in both directions. The citizen pays government. Government must deliver.

Nigeria's middle class is under enormous pressure. The civil servant, teacher, professional and small shop owner confront food, transportation, housing, healthcare and electricity costs that consume larger portions of household income. It would be inaccurate to say literally that no Nigerian middle class remains, but its purchasing power has been severely squeezed. An economy needs a functioning middle class because these households consume, save, invest, employ people and support domestic businesses. When they become poorer, the damage travels through the economy.

We claim to be a free democratic republic, yet Nigeria has repeatedly faced serious disputes over the treatment of peaceful protesters and critics of government. Democracy must protect peaceful disagreement within the law. Citizens must be able to criticise those governing them without political disagreement itself becoming criminalised. Independence is not simply the freedom of government to govern. It is also the freedom of citizens to question government.

Our manufacturing sector faces foreign-exchange pressures, expensive energy, financing constraints and infrastructure deficiencies. When a factory closes, the consequences do not end at its gate. A worker loses a salary. A supplier loses an order. A transporter loses business. A family loses income. Government loses tax revenue. Nigeria cannot consume its way into prosperity. Economic independence ultimately requires producing substantially more of what we consume and creating productive work for our growing population.
Where is the empathy in governance? People can endure difficult reforms when they understand why the sacrifice is necessary, can see where it leads and believe those governing them are sharing the burden. Leadership requires leading by example, not merely asking citizens for patience. Public trust suffers when there is a visible gulf between the austerity demanded from ordinary households and the lifestyle they associate with political office.
Temporary cash transfers and emergency palliatives can help vulnerable Nigerians survive severe shocks. But slapping temporary relief on structural economic failures is like putting a bandage on a deep wound. Palliatives cannot substitute for reliable electricity, secure farmlands, productive employment, functioning schools and hospitals, competitive industries, efficient infrastructure, reduced oil losses and disciplined government expenditure. A bag of rice can relieve today's hunger. It cannot become tomorrow's economic policy.
Finally, symbolic celebrations cannot cover our national agony. The Federal Government cancelled the central Independence Anniversary parade in 2025, although its official announcement did not attribute the cancellation to security threats or low public enthusiasm. We should not invent a reason where government did not provide one. But the deeper question survives regardless of whether a parade holds: what does independence mean if millions of citizens cannot feel its benefits in their ordinary lives?
These are twenty questions and twenty reasons behind our argument that Nigeria needs a change of government in 2027. They are the reasons behind the call to send Tinubu out of the Villa and bring in His Excellency Atiku Abubakar. These are questions Nigeria cannot silence with fireworks, flags or speeches. Our argument is that if Tinubu and the APC remain in power past 2027 and these conditions continue, the economic despair could deepen further, leaving even more young Nigerians dreaming not of building a life at home, but of London, Canada or anywhere they believe offers an escape from hardship.
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) does not ask for your vote based on cheap slogans. Our case is that we offer a structured, compassionate and realistic alternative: a government that secures farmlands, protects the naira, invests in human capital and halts the wasteful extravagance of political elites. Nigerians must examine that offer, interrogate it and compare it with the record of those currently in power.
For those making the case for political change, the ballot box is the ultimate democratic weapon. The argument is simple: your PVC is your constitutional instrument for holding Tinubu, the APC and every other political leader accountable.

text:
Joey Porter Jr. was a good football player. That’s not really the argument. The question is whether he was worth the price he wanted — reportedly north of $30 million per year — and whether Pittsburgh was wrong to move on when the two sides couldn’t reach an agreement...
Let’s actually look at the player rather than turning this into a personal argument....
In 2025, Porter played 14 games and produced 52 tackles, 14 passes defended, one interception and one sack. He did not allow a receiving touchdown. His coverage numbers were legitimately impressive: 66 targets, 32 completions, 333 yards allowed and a 57.2 passer rating against according to Pro Football Reference...
Next Gen Stats also had him allowing only 32 receptions on 64 targets, with zero touchdowns and a 61.5 passer rating in 524 coverage snaps..
So yes — there was real value there.
But there was another part of the evaluation that can't simply be ignored.
Penalties...
Porter had nine accepted penalties in 2025, including five defensive pass-interference calls and two defensive-holding penalties, according to Steelers Depot's review of PFF data. That was a substantial improvement from his 17 penalties in 2024, but it remained part of his game.
And this wasn't some isolated issue against lesser competition...
Against Cincinnati in Week 7 of 2025, Porter was charged with two penalties while allowing 37 yards on four catches and seven targets. In the second Cincinnati meeting, however, he allowed zero catches on three targets with no penalty...
That pretty much tells the story of Porter: he had the ability to play elite receivers and shut them down, but his physical style also created unnecessary risk...
And that's where the contract discussion matters...
Over his first three seasons, Porter accumulated 31 passes defended and three interceptions, while allowing a 71.2 career passer rating in coverage according to PFR. A July 2026 Steelers Depot analysis comparing him with highly paid corners had his three-year average at a 54.3 passer rating against and 45.9% catch rate allowed, both among the best figures in that comparison group..
So I'm not going to pretend Pittsburgh traded away some scrub..
They traded away a talented, physical corner who had legitimate shutdown stretches...
But there's a difference between saying "Joey Porter Jr. is a good corner" and saying "Joey Porter Jr. is worth resetting the cornerback market at $30+ million per year."..
That's the part I can't blame the Steelers for questioning...
Pittsburgh reportedly offered a contract worth slightly more than $27 million annually, which would have made Porter one of the highest-paid cornerbacks in football. Porter reportedly wanted more than $30 million annually. The two sides never reached an agreement...
Then came 2026...
Porter didn't play the Steelers' first three games. He was dealing with a back/conditioning situation while the contract dispute remained unresolved. Pittsburgh ultimately traded him to Dallas for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick...
And that's the part people need to separate from emotion...
Pittsburgh didn't have to decide whether Joey Porter Jr. was talented enough to keep...
He was...
They had to decide whether they wanted to commit elite-corner money to a player entering the final year of his rookie contract, while also dealing with an unresolved contract standoff...
There is nothing wrong with Porter believing he was worth $30+ million.
There is also nothing wrong with the Steelers deciding they weren't going to pay it....
Sometimes the best roster decision isn't about whether a player is good enough...
It's about whether the player, the price, the role and the situation still make sense together...
And once the relationship reaches the point where the player wants one number and the organization has drawn a line somewhere else, moving on can be better than forcing the relationship to continue.................
