text:
On this day in history - October 1, 1908 

The first production Model T Ford is completed at the company’s Piquette Avenue plant in Detroit. Between 1908 and 1927, Ford would build some 15 million Model T cars. It was the longest production run of any automobile model in history until the Volkswagen Beetle surpassed it in 1972.

Before the Model T, cars were a luxury item: At the beginning of 1908, there were fewer than 200,000 on the road. Though the Model T was fairly expensive at first (the cheapest one initially cost $825, or about $18,000 in today’s dollars), it was built for ordinary people to drive every day. It had a 22-horsepower, four-cylinder engine and was made of a new kind of heat-treated steel, pioneered by French race car makers, that made it lighter (it weighed just 1,200 pounds) and stronger than its predecessors had been. It could go as fast as 40 miles per hour and could run on gasoline or hemp-based fuel. (When oil prices dropped in the early 20th century, making gasoline more affordable, Ford phased out the hemp option.)  “No car under $2,000 offers more,” ads crowed, “and no car over $2,000 offers more except the trimmings.”

Ford kept prices low by sticking to a single product. By building just one model, for example, the company’s engineers could develop a system of interchangeable parts that reduced waste, saved time and made it easy for unskilled workers to assemble the cars. By 1914, the moving assembly line made it possible to produce thousands of cars every week and by 1924, workers at the River Rouge Ford plant in Dearborn, Michigan could cast more than 10,000 Model T cylinder blocks in a day.

But by the 1920s, many Americans wanted more than just a sturdy, affordable car. They wanted style (for many years, the Model T famously came in just one color: black), speed and luxury too. As tastes changed, the era of the Model T came to an end and the last one rolled off the assembly line on May 26, 1927.

text:
"My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?

Why so far from my call for help, from my cries of anguish?

Yet you are enthroned as the Holy One; you are the glory of Israel.

In you our fathers trusted; they trusted and you rescued them.

But I am a worm, not a man,
scorned by men, despised by the people.

All who see me mock me; they curl their lips and jeer; they shake their heads at me:

"He relied on the Lord
-let him deliver him;
if he loves him, let him rescue him."

For you drew me forth from the womb, made me safe at my mother's breasts.

Upon you I was thrust from the womb; since my mother bore me you are my God.

Do not stay far from me, for trouble is near,
and there is no one to help.

Many bulls surround me;
fierce bulls of Bashan encircle me.

They open their mouths against me, lions that rend and roar.

Like water my life drains away; all my bones are disjointed.
My heart has become like wax, it melts away within me.

As dry as a potsherd is my throat; my tongue cleaves to my palate; you lay me in the dust of death.

Dogs surround me;
a pack of evildoers closes in on me.

They have pierced my hands and my feet

I can count all my bones.
They stare at me and gloat;

they divide my garments among them; for my clothing they cast lots.

But you, Lord,
do not stay far off;

my strength, come quickly to help me.

Deliver my soul from the sword, my life from the grip of the dog.

"You who fear the Lord give praise!
All descendants of Jacob, give honor; show reverence, all descendants of Israel!

For he has not spurned or disdained the misery of this poor wretch, Did not turn away from me, but heard me when I cried out.

I will offer praise in the great assembly; my vows I will fulfill before those who fear him.

May your hearts enjoy life forever!"
All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord;

All the families of nations will bow low before him.

For kingship belongs to the Lord, the ruler over the nations.
All who sleep in the earth will bow low before God;

All who have gone down into the dust will kneel in homage."

text:
On October 1, 1910, a massive explosion destroys the Los Angeles Times building in the city’s downtown area, killing 21 and injuring many more. Since Los Angeles Times publisher Harrison Otis, a virulent opponent of unions, believed that the bomb was directed at him, he hired the nation’s premier private detective, William J. Burns, to crack the case. In addition to printing numerous editorials against unions, Otis was the leader of the Merchants and Manufacturing Association, a powerful group of business owners with extensive political connections.

Burns’ investigation led him to the Bridge and Structural Iron Workers Union and their treasurer, John J. McNamara. In April 1911, after Burns got a confession out of Ortie McManigal, who had allegedly been the intermediary between McNamara and two bomb experts, he personally arrested John McNamara and his brother in Indiana. Without any legal authority, Burns also managed to get the brothers to California, where they were to be prosecuted.

Union members and left-wing supporters rallied around the McNamara brothers. After a large defense fund was raised, union representatives pleaded with Clarence Darrow to take the case. Darrow, who was the best defense attorney America had to offer, had already gotten “Big Bill” Haywood, the union leader of the Industrial Workers of the World, off on murder charges in Idaho a few years earlier. Offered $50,000, he reluctantly took the case.

text:
A drug's crystal structure once forced a total product recall, and this company is betting zero gravity can prevent the next one.

Varda Space, an in-space manufacturing startup based in El Segundo, California, raised $250 million in a Series D round at a $1.6 billion valuation, led by Lux Capital and Natural Capital, bringing its total funding to $598 million since founding in 2021. The company builds uncrewed capsules that function as orbital manufacturing platforms, with pharmaceuticals as its main commercial focus.

The pitch rests on a real materials science problem. Without gravity driven convection and sedimentation, molecular crystals can form more evenly, which matters because a drug's exact crystal structure, called its polymorph, directly affects how well it dissolves and how stable it stays in storage.

This is not a hypothetical risk. In 1998, Abbott Laboratories ($ABT) had to pull its HIV drug ritonavir from the market after a new, far less soluble crystal form began appearing in production, essentially overwhelming the original form and making existing capsules ineffective. The incident disrupted treatment for HIV patients and reportedly cost the company on the order of hundreds of millions of dollars to resolve. Varda has already flown a mission specifically to grow a different polymorph of that exact same drug, ritonavir, in orbit, which is about as direct an answer to that old crisis as a company can offer.

Varda has 28 launches booked with different providers through 2027 to 2029, which insulates it from the industry's broader launch bottleneck, and expects roughly 70% of next year's customers to be government agencies rather than pharmaceutical companies. Not every mission has gone smoothly either. Of its capsules flown so far, one failed to return successfully. The company also competes with SpaceX's ($SPCX) newer Starfall program and a startup called Inversion Space, both chasing overlapping opportunities in orbital manufacturing and fast cargo delivery.

Private investment in space companies reached roughly $23 billion in the year through June, more than double the year before, so this round rides a much larger wave of capital, not an isolated bet.

If putting drug manufacturing in orbit can genuinely address a problem that has already caused a real recall, how much of a valuation premium does that justify for a company that has not scaled commercial production yet?

Do you remember Saul also known as Paul from the Bible? Do you believe people can change? 

The narrative is that Christa Pike has not been a model prisoner and has not repented and isn’t remorseful. She has done both many times. And here’s the truth about the last few years in prison after she got on lithium to treat her bipolar. 

Although Christa’s surroundings have changed very little during her incarceration, Christa has changed significantly. Christa has become a lifeline for other inmates.

Marcy Graves’ daughter, Teddy, became addicted to prescription drugs after being diagnosed with a serious heart condition. 

After Teddy was arrested, the Houston County jail transferred her to the women’s prison as a safekeeper because it could not accommodate her health condition. Teddy was housed in Unit 3, just across from Christa.

Marcy was terrified that her daughter was held next to Christa, whose case and crime details Marcy had followed. She thought Christa was evil. Marcy worried for her timid and small daughter—Teddy had never been in trouble before. Marcy warned Teddy to stay away from Christa.

As Teddy was escorted to the shower the first time, she heard Christa’s voice coming through her pie flap, “You better not get in that shower with no shower shoes, girl!” A few minutes later, an officer handed Teddy a new pair of shower shoes. “Love, Christa Pike” was written in sharpie on the sole. 

Marcy was still frightened and worried.  As Teddy waited three months to receive a property package with clothing and other necessities, Christa helped Teddy obtain what she needed. She even gave the officers her own radio, headphones, pencils, and paper to bring to Teddy to help her pass the time. If Teddy was sick, Christa would advocate for her until the officers got a nurse to attend to Teddy.

Marcy had only seen how the media portrayed Christa. She learned Christa’s true nature through the letters Marcy and Christa began to write regularly. Christa helped Teddy through her time on Unit 3 and has helped Marcy through her own difficulties,Teddy’s release from prison, and Teddy’s death. Marcy and Christa became friends and talk often. Christa named the chickens on Marcy’s farm and painted pictures of mermaids for Marcy’s home. 

This is how Marcy now describes Christa, the person she once feared: 

“This woman Christa gave all she had to give to a perfect stranger who was scared, sick and alone in a very scary place. Christa loved, befriended, fed, clothed, and cared for my child when I could not reach her. She eased my heart, the heart of a terrified, worried mother.  Christa is a beautiful soul who did a really bad thing when she was very young. She is not that person anymore.”

Teddy is not the only woman Christa has helped. Over and over, new, vulnerable women arrive on Unit 3 and Christa comforts them and meets their basic needs. She has provided toiletries, hygiene products, paper, and food to innumerable new arrivals. 

Ashlee Sellars was one of those women. She was transferred into the adult system as a teenager in 1995 and received a letter from Christa. She had never met Christa and was unfamiliar with her story. 

Christa’s letter offered encouragement. She told her, “Don’t be afraid, there are people who will look out for you.” She and Christa were housed near each other for a time. They would kneel at their pie flaps and talk. 

Kasey Raines who was sent to TPFW as a pregnant young woman struggling with addiction. Christa supported and encouraged her; she made sure Kasey and her growing baby had proper nutrition.  

Kasey said: “I was three hours from my family, I was scared, I had nothing. Nothing to do besides cry and write on free paper they had given me. It was probably one of the most darkest times of my life honestly. (Continued in replies)

$SPX $SPY $QQQ $IGV $IWM 

DLMM PREMARKET INTELLIGENCE
Thursday, October 1, 2026
Data checked: 7:30 AM ET
Market snapshot time range: 7:19 AM–7:30 AM ET

MARKET TONE

ES: 7,729.75, +14.25 points (+0.18%). Overnight range: 7,705.00–7,767.75. ES is green but sits below the overnight high after a meaningful two-way range. Buyers have not yet earned acceptance above 7,767.75; sellers have not yet taken back 7,705.00.

NQ: 30,841.00, +142.25 points (+0.46%). Overnight range: 30,684.50–31,151.50. NQ leads ES on percentage terms, but the contract has retraced substantially from its overnight high. That makes 31,151.50 the decision point rather than a breakout already in progress.

RTY: 2,815.40, -2.10 points (-0.07%). Overnight range: 2,797.90–2,835.20. Small caps are not participating in the NQ bid. That divergence matters: index strength is presently being carried by the larger growth complex rather than broad participation.

VIX: 16.41, +0.07 (+0.43%).
DXY: 101.85, +0.40 (+0.39%).
Front-month WTI: 92.26, +1.84 (+2.03%). Overnight range: 88.79–92.90.
Gold futures: 4,197.30, +10.60 (+0.25%). Overnight range: 4,169.40–4,222.80.
Bitcoin: 83,834.06, +280.21 (+0.34%). Overnight range: 83,130.76–84,368.26.

The active equity-index futures cycle is December 2026. The ES, NQ, and RTY levels above remain futures levels; do not substitute ETF or cash-index prices for those references.

CONFIRMED TONE: Modestly risk-on index pricing led by NQ, but the tape is internally uneven. Oil, the dollar, and gold are all higher while RTY is red. That is not clean, broad risk appetite.

DLMM READ: The overnight tape says buyers can defend tech, but it does not yet say they control the entire market. NQ is the strongest contract, ES is constructive but trapped inside a broad overnight range, and RTY is the weak link. Respect the opening reaction. A green futures print alone is not alignment.

WHY IT MATTERS
First force: technology leadership is real, but it is selective.

NQ is up 0.46%, more than twice the ES gain, while RTY is lower. That is a clear price-performance split. Semiconductor and semiconductor-equipment rotation are also near the top of the 20-day range universe, reinforcing the case that traders should look first to large-cap technology and chip-related names if the open confirms strength.

The interpretation: a strong NQ with flat-to-red RTY can still produce clean upside trades, but it narrows the number of acceptable long candidates. It also raises the bar for broad-index longs. If NQ fails its opening push while RTY cannot improve, the market has less internal support than the headline futures print suggests.

Second force: the overnight range already contains the first battle.

ES traveled from 7,705.00 to 7,767.75, a 62.75-point overnight range. NQ traveled from 30,684.50 to 31,151.50, a 467.00-point range. Neither contract is opening at an extreme. That means both sides have already shown they can move price.

The interpretation: the highest-quality opening trade is not at the middle. It comes if price accepts outside an overnight boundary or rejects a boundary and then fails the retest. Middle-of-range participation is where traders get chopped while waiting for one side to surrender.

Third force: oil is a live cross-market complication.

WTI is up 2.03% and traded as high as 92.90 overnight. DXY is also higher, while gold is green. Those concurrent moves keep inflation and geopolitical risk in the background even as NQ bids. The confirmed fact is the price behavior across those markets. The informed interpretation is that a continued oil push can pressure the broad tape or limit upside follow-through if it begins to change the reaction in equities after the open.
Do not predict that relationship. Trade it only if price confirms it: ES and NQ failing their highs while energy holds its bid is evidence; an oil headline without equity structure is not a trade.

Fourth force: scheduled data can create the first real decision candles.

TODAY’S EVENTS:
8:30 AM ET: Initial Jobless Claims.
10:00 AM ET: ISM Manufacturing PMI for September.
10:00 AM ET: Construction Spending.
11:30 AM ET: Weekly Economic Index.

The 8:30 AM ET release lands before the cash open and can alter the character of the opening gap. The 10:00 AM ET cluster arrives after the first 30 minutes, when opening-range traders are often already committed. That is a reason to avoid forcing a marginal entry just before 10:00 AM ET. If price is compressed into that time, wait for the reaction and trade the decision candle—not the forecast.

ROTATION MAP

Participation is NARROW.

The 18-ETF rotation universe does not show broad upside alignment. Two groups clearly separate at the top, several are mixed and mid-range, and a large portion of the universe remains near 20-day lows or carries negative short- and medium-term price performance.

Leading rotation:

Lithography and semiconductor equipment, represented by EUV, is the top-ranked group. It is up 3.10% over five sessions and 8.13% over 21 sessions, sitting at 94.50% of its 20-day range. The 20-day high is 25.47. This is leadership, but it is also near an obvious decision area. Do not buy it because it is high in the range; buy only if it accepts above a key intraday level or rejects and reclaims support.
Semiconductors, represented by SMH, are the cleanest large liquid leadership group. SMH is up 1.26% over five sessions and 9.41% over 21 sessions, sitting at 94.30% of its 20-day range with a 20-day high of 613.27. That aligns with NQ leadership. The opening question is whether the group can hold strength after the first pullback. If it can, semiconductor-related names deserve priority. If it loses the opening drive and cannot reclaim it, do not assume the prior trend will rescue a poor entry.

Cybersecurity, represented by CIBR, is near the upper end of its 20-day range at 90.00% and retains strong 63-day price performance of 13.15%, though its five-day performance is negative. That is not fresh leadership; it is a constructive longer structure that needs a new higher low or a reclaim before it becomes actionable.

Quantum computing, represented by QTUM, is 75.50% through its 20-day range. Its five-day performance is slightly negative, while its 21-day performance is positive. This is a mixed continuation structure, not an immediate broad-theme green light.

Memory, represented by DRAM, is also mixed. It is down 2.49% over five sessions but up 6.08% over 21 sessions and sits at 63.70% of its 20-day range. Memory can provide individual opportunities, but the group needs to prove it can stop making lower intraday highs before it belongs in the lead basket.

Middle and mixed rotation:

Software, represented by IGV, sits at 75.00% of its 20-day range and has strong 63-day price performance, but it is down over both five and 21 sessions. This is not synchronized with semiconductors. A software long needs its own reaction; it cannot borrow confirmation from SMH.

Robotics and automation, BOTZ, is near the middle of its range at 49.70%, with negative 21-day and 63-day price performance. There is no leadership case until price reclaims structure.
Healthcare, XLV, is at 35.30% of its 20-day range. Grid and electrification, GRID, is at 47.30%. Space and innovation, ARKX, is at 35.40%. These are mixed-to-weak rotations. They can bounce, but they are not where traders should begin looking for sustained upside unless the opening tape produces a clear reversal and the broader market supports it.

Weak rotation:

Energy, XLE, is at just 10.50% of its 20-day range despite the current bid in WTI. That divergence is important. Oil strength has not yet translated into a confirmed energy-equity leadership structure. Do not assume an oil move automatically makes XLE a long.

Small caps, IWM, are at 2.60% of their 20-day range. Financials, XLF, are at 0.60%. Data centers and digital infrastructure, DTCR, are at 6.20%. Copper miners, COPX, are at 11.90%. Aerospace and defense, ITA, are at 1.50%. Nuclear and uranium, NLR, are at 1.80%.

These groups are structurally weak relative to the rest of the universe. They are the first places to look for failed bounces if ES loses 7,705.00 and RTY cannot reclaim its opening range. But low range location is not itself a short entry. A short requires a failed reclaim, a lower high, or candle-body acceptance beneath a defined intraday level.

Bitcoin miners, WGMI, deserve separate treatment. The group is down 9.76% over five sessions, yet Bitcoin is modestly green overnight. That is a conflict. Bitcoin strength alone does not repair a weak miner structure. Require the miner group itself to reclaim and hold before assigning it upside continuation.

LEADERS & LAGGARDS

There are no verified fresh individual premarket movers or company-specific catalysts in the current view. Do not manufacture a catalyst narrative from premarket bids and offers.

The leadership list is therefore structural, not a claim about fresh company news:
Semiconductors and lithography/equipment are the leading rotations, supported by SMH and EUV sitting above 94% of their respective 20-day ranges.

Cybersecurity and quantum are secondary watch groups: their range positions are constructive, but recent price performance is less decisive.

The laggard list is also structural:

Financials, small caps, nuclear/uranium, aerospace/defense, data-center infrastructure, copper miners, and energy are all located near the lower end of their respective 20-day ranges.

The practical distinction: leaders deserve attention on accepted breakouts and defended pullbacks. Laggards deserve attention only on failed bounces or genuine reversal structures. Do not short a weak group at the low, and do not long a strong group after it has already extended without a new decision candle.

DLMM TRADE MAP

BULLISH SCENARIO

The clean bullish path begins with ES holding above 7,705.00 after the cash open, then building candle-body acceptance above 7,729.75. Stronger confirmation comes if ES breaks 7,767.75, closes a decision candle above it, and holds that level on the first retest.

NQ must participate. A valid risk-on expansion requires NQ to reclaim and hold above 30,841.00, then show acceptance through 31,151.50. If ES is green but NQ cannot hold its opening push, the best long names will be less forgiving.

RTY does not need to lead, but it should stop making lower highs and ideally reclaim 2,815.40. A move through 2,835.20 would improve broad participation. Without that, keep long exposure concentrated in the strongest technology groups rather than treating the tape as universally bullish.

BEARISH SCENARIO
The bearish path starts if ES tests 7,767.75 and rejects it with a clear upper wick, then loses 7,729.75 with candle-body acceptance below. The stronger downside confirmation is a failed reclaim of 7,705.00 followed by sustained trade beneath that overnight low.

NQ needs to confirm by failing beneath 30,841.00 and then accepting below 30,684.50. If NQ holds while ES slips, be selective with shorts; that can be sector rotation rather than broad surrender.

RTY is the downside confirmation contract. A failed reclaim of 2,815.40 followed by acceptance under 2,797.90 would keep the weak breadth message intact. In that case, failed bounces in IWM, XLF, and structurally weak groups carry more logic than chasing downside in the strongest semiconductor names.

CHOP / NO-TRADE SCENARIO

No pattern, no trade.

Expect chop if ES remains between 7,705.00 and 7,767.75 while NQ stays inside 30,684.50–31,151.50 and RTY remains trapped below 2,835.20. The middle of the overnight range is not an edge.

Also stand down if ES and NQ disagree: ES pushes higher while NQ fails, or NQ pushes higher while ES and RTY reject. That is misalignment. Wait for one side to surrender and for the next candle to prove whether the break holds.

NAMES ON THE SCREEN

CONDITIONAL LONG BIAS

NVDA — Semiconductor leadership and NQ strength place it near the top of the list. Require an opening hold above its prior cash close of 228.38, followed by a higher low and a reclaim of the opening-range high. No chase if it extends before building a base.

AMD — Same group alignment as NVDA, with a prior cash close of 611.76. The requirement is an opening reclaim and hold above that reference, ideally with SMH holding its first pullback. If AMD cannot hold the opening range while SMH is firm, that relative weakness matters.
WDC — Memory is mixed, but the broader semiconductor complex is strong. Prior cash close: 454.46. Long only if it establishes acceptance above the opening range and does not immediately fail back beneath the prior close.

SMCI — A high-beta semiconductor-infrastructure name that can respond to NQ direction. Prior cash close: 41.07. Require a clean higher low after the open and a break that holds. If it repeatedly wicks above resistance and closes back below, leave it alone.

CONDITIONAL SHORT BIAS

INTC — Prior cash close: 120.23. Its current indication is below that reference while the semiconductor group itself is strong, creating a possible relative-weakness setup. Short only on a failed reclaim of 120.23 with a lower high. Do not press it if the broader chip group is accepting higher.

IWM — Small caps are near the bottom of the rotation map and RTY is red overnight. Prior cash close: 277.89. Short only if it fails to hold a reclaim of that reference and RTY remains below 2,815.40. If RTY recovers and holds, remove the short thesis.

XLF — Financials are at the lowest range location in the full rotation universe. Prior cash close: 53.40. The short setup is a bounce that fails beneath 53.40 or an opening breakdown followed by a failed retest. Avoid initiating at the low without a failed bounce.

TWO-WAY NAMES

MU — Memory has positive 21-day performance but negative five-day performance. Prior cash close: 1,065.11. Above-and-hold behavior through the opening range can align it with semiconductor strength; a failed reclaim of the prior close can create a short-side rotation trade. Let price choose the side.
PLTR — Prior cash close: 187.05. It has a positive premarket indication but lacks a supplied fresh company-specific catalyst. Treat it as a reaction name: long only on accepted opening strength and a defended higher low; short only if the opening push fails and price accepts below the prior close.

TSLA — Prior cash close: 354.81. This is a two-way name because it can move independently of index tone. Require a clean opening-range break, a retest, and a hold. If it remains inside the opening range while ES and NQ disagree, it is a pass.

BOTTOM LINE

The overnight market is constructive, not cleanly broad. NQ and semiconductor rotation lead. ES is positive but remains below its overnight high. RTY, financials, and small caps are not confirming the upside message.

The best upside conditions are ES acceptance above 7,767.75 with NQ holding above 31,151.50 and at least stabilization from RTY. That would keep the focus on semiconductors, selective technology, and names that build higher lows after the open.

The best downside conditions are rejection at the overnight highs, loss of ES 7,705.00, and NQ acceptance below 30,684.50. That would validate failed-bounce shorts in weak rotation groups rather than indiscriminate downside chasing.

Until then, this is a reaction market. Look left. Trade the response at the level. Let candle bodies—not headlines, assumptions, or the first green print—tell you whether buyers or sellers have actually surrendered.

American Airlines AAdvantage cards include free first checked bag. Southwest's Rapid Rewards cards include 2 free checked bags."

"But the benefit only works if you purchase the ticket with that card — and are listed on the reservation. If you booked with a different card, or through a third party, the benefit might not apply."

"The 24-hour rule — the DOT regulation that lets you cancel any flight within 24 hours for a full refund — applies to tickets booked directly with the airline. Third-party sites have their own cancellation policies. Most are worse."

🛡️ CYBER BULLETIN | 2026/10/01 🚨

1) Cisco SD-WAN Manager auth bypass is in the KEV
CVE-2026-76504 (CVSS 9.8) lets an unauthenticated attacker reach the Manager API as admin by slipping a URI-encoded character past the login rule. Cisco PSIRT says it saw exploitation in September. No workaround. First fixed builds: 20.9.10.1, 20.12.8.2, 20.15.6.1, 20.18.4.1, 26.1.2.1, 26.2.1. CISA added it on 30 Sep. CSIRT Italia issued AL10/260930 the same day.

2) Pentagon HR system breach hit more than 3 million people
DMDC letters say unauthorized users reached a file-sharing system from October 2025 to July 2026. Stolen fields vary and include SSNs, names, dates of birth, contact data, and military personnel info. Pentagon officials put the count at nearly 2.8 million living people and 294,000 deceased. Twelve months of credit monitoring is offered.

3) MetaMask exits Ethereum validators after an infra incident
MetaMask says an ongoing incident affects part of its infrastructure and that it sees no immediate threat to wallets. It is pulling affected validators from its non-custodial staking setup and does not hold withdrawal keys. Lido says the last exits should finish by 7 Oct, with missed rewards and possible downtime penalties.

4) Microsoft maps Zimbra CVE-2026-73570 webshells
A crafted email can hit the SNMP notification path when zimbra-snmp is installed and notifications are on, and run commands as the zimbra user. Microsoft saw JSP webshells, reverse shells, and mailbox archive staging between the 20 Jul patch (10.1.20) and the 13 Aug disclosure. CISA put it on the KEV in August.

5) Star Blizzard ships CosmicPulse through RedFlick
Microsoft says the Russian group sends a password-protected archive with a VHDX and an LNK disguised as a PDF. Opening it sets three scheduled tasks, then a .cpl downloader (NOROBOT/BAITSWITCH) fetches the Python CosmicPulse backdoor. Since January it has run at least 13 campaigns against more than 100 orgs, mostly in the US and UK, plus Ukrainian targets and groups that support Ukraine.

text:
Open letter to @USAA and Juan Andrade:

I have been a member since my Air Force Academy cadet days in the early 1990s. I used to use USAA for all my financial needs. Checking, credit card, mortgage, investing, life, auto, home, umbrella. This morning I moved the last of the insurance to Amica. I am down to a credit card I keep alive with a small monthly charge so it stays on my credit report.

You lost the investing first. Vanguard was not close on fees.

You lost the checking next. I used to brag about that account. You reimbursed ATM fees and you were early on mobile deposit. Fidelity Cash Management beats both USAA checking and a high-yield savings account. One account does both jobs.

You lost the card after that. I will pay a few hundred dollars a year for primary rental-car coverage. You never offered a card in that class. I would have switched back. I still have the old USAA card. I put one small charge on it so the account stays open. I do not use it.

Insurance is why I am writing, and why I left. When my term life expired, your price was almost 3 times Pacific Life on a 15-year policy. I took Pacific Life.

This year you were about to double my umbrella, and nobody could tell me why. I called. Four people, then a disconnect. Same thing on a glass claim last year. Nobody owned it, and I paid more out of pocket than I should have.

Then you put points on our auto policy for tickets that are not on the records. I called. You sent me to LexisNexis. LexisNexis said both of my sons were clean. You sent me to the Florida DHSMV and the Illinois Secretary of State. I pulled both official records. Valid licenses. No tickets. No points. More than an hour getting the documents, then another half hour on the phone trying to hand them to someone at USAA. That should not be what it takes for a 30-year member to fix points you assessed in error.

So I left. Auto, home, and umbrella are with Amica as of this morning.

I am sad about it. I did not want to leave. You spent decades building a reputation I used to defend, and I am sorry to watch it go, one product at a time, on phone calls nobody owns.

Start with customer service. Gut it and rebuild it, and put members first again. Cut the products that are not core, and cut the marketing. I hope you do. If you do not, the case studies will sit you next to Kodak and Southwest.

Proposed Kenya Spaceport Project: Advancing Strategic Public Investment and Infrastructure Development.

The State Department for Public Investments and Assets Management (SDPIAM), through the @ppp_kenya (PPP) Directorate, is supporting the development of the proposed Kenya Spaceport Project as a strategic infrastructure investment aimed at unlocking new economic opportunities, mobilising private-sector capital and strengthening Kenya’s long-term asset base.

The PPP Directorate General, @EngKefaSeda, hosted the Director General of the  @SpaceAgencyKE (KSA), Major General Hillary Kipkosgey, for the signing of a funding agreement to facilitate the feasibility study for the proposed spaceport. 

The signing follows the appointment of a Transaction Advisor to undertake comprehensive technical, commercial and financial assessments and provide specialised advisory support towards establishing a viable and bankable project structure.

The proposed spaceport presents an opportunity to leverage Kenya’s strategic geographic position along the equator and its east-facing coastline, which offers potential advantages for space-launch operations. The project can also build on existing and planned investments in enabling infrastructure within the coastal region, including transport, energy, water and port facilities, thereby promoting integrated and efficient utilisation of public infrastructure and assets.

From a public investment and assets management perspective, the feasibility study will be critical in determining the most appropriate investment and delivery structure, assessing project risks and returns, and establishing mechanisms that safeguard public interest while attracting private capital. 

The Transaction Advisor will also support the development of a competitive process for selecting a private-sector partner, with emphasis on value for money, affordability, risk allocation and sustainable management of the resulting strategic asset.

Beyond its infrastructure dimension, the spaceport is expected to contribute to Kenya’s industrialisation and economic transformation by stimulating investment in the space economy, creating employment and business opportunities, promoting technology and skills development, and strengthening local capabilities in high-value sectors. 

A commercially viable spaceport could also generate additional Government revenues through appropriate revenue-sharing arrangements.
The project therefore demonstrates the Government’s approach to transforming public investments and strategic assets into productive economic enablers while leveraging private-sector expertise and financing.

 Through PPPs, SDPIAM continues to support the development of infrastructure that delivers value for money, strengthens public asset utilisation and contributes to efficient, sustainable and citizen-centred service delivery.

The Kenya Spaceport Project is consequently positioned not only as an investment in space infrastructure, but as a strategic public asset with the potential to support economic diversification, enhance national competitiveness and contribute to Kenya’s long-term development objectives.

text:
Veteran Tory joins the movement that beat him

Restore Britain’s local arm in Great Yarmouth, Norfolk, has today won over long-standing Conservative councillor James Bensly, cutting the Tory group to 17 seats and leaving Labour the council’s largest party on 18.

The striking part is not simply that another councillor has changed colours.

Bensly has sat in the Conservative cabinet at Great Yarmouth Borough Council for years, representing East Flegg and dealing with the hard, visible problems of a coastline where homes have been lost to erosion.

He was not watching Rupert Lowe’s operation from a safe distance.

In May, Bensly stood for the Conservatives in The Fleggs division at the Norfolk county election and was beaten by Great Yarmouth First candidate Jason Hughes.

The result was not close: Hughes took 1,895 votes, while Bensly received 866.

Across Rupert Lowe’s constituency, Great Yarmouth First-the local party aligned with Restore Britain-won every one of the ten seats it contested.

That was the first turn.

The man who had held the county seat under the old party label had just been defeated by the local movement many Westminster observers had treated as an experiment.

Four months later, Bensly has crossed the floor to join it.

He says Britain needs fundamental changes in how it is governed, with less needless bureaucracy and a system that listens to ordinary people and delivers for them.

Those words carry extra weight in Hemsby, near Great Yarmouth, where residents have watched the sea take roads and force homes to be demolished while officials argue over what can be funded.

Rupert Lowe calls Bensly a local champion for Hemsby and says the move is a massive boost to Restore Britain’s ambitions.

The Conservatives accuse Bensly of putting ambition before principle, while the report says he is understood to have been offered a chance to stand for Restore Britain in Lowestoft at the next general election.

But the political consequence is already real, whatever rivals say about motive.

Great Yarmouth’s Conservatives still run the authority, yet they now do so as a smaller minority in a council with no overall control.

That gives Restore Britain and the remaining independents more weight whenever the larger groups split.

This is how Rupert Lowe’s project moves from speeches to power: first it beats an established councillor, then it persuades him that the old parties cannot deliver the change his coastal communities need.

The final image is hard to miss.

The Conservative who lost to Rupert Lowe’s local movement is now helping it decide what happens next.

text:
YouTube has paid creators over $100 billion since 2021. Every challenger that tried to match that check is dead.

Quibi raised $1.75 billion before launch, one of the biggest war chests in startup history, and folded in six months. YouTube pays out roughly that much to creators every single month.

Vine is the cleanest autopsy. Back in 2016, about 20 of its biggest stars offered to keep posting in exchange for $1.2 million each. Vine said no. They took their audiences to YouTube and Instagram, and Vine shut down within the year.

Here's why nobody breaks through. Video is the most expensive content on the internet to serve, so a challenger bleeds money on infrastructure for years before ads can work. YouTube itself didn't clearly make money for close to a decade after Google bought it for $1.65 billion in 2006, a deal people called the dumbest in tech. In 2025 it did over $60 billion.

Only Google could afford that wait, because search profits covered the losses. And once YouTube could fund a 55% revenue share, creators became the defense budget. Beating YouTube was never a product problem. You'd have to outbid $22 billion a year in creator checks with no ad machine to pay for it.

Twenty years in, nobody has even tried twice.

text:
🔔 TODAY THE CHURCH CELEBRATES
St. Thérèse of Lisieux
October 1

🕊️ WHAT WE REMEMBER
St. Thérèse was a Carmelite nun and Doctor of the Church who sought holiness through her “Little Way” - trusting God completely and doing small, ordinary things with great love.

🔥 WHY IT MATTERS
St. Thérèse reminds us that holiness is not only found in extraordinary acts. Even the smallest things, when offered to God with love, can become a path to sainthood.

👣 HOW WE LIVE IT
Choose one ordinary task today and do it with extra love, patience or kindness. Let something small become an offering to God.

🙏 TODAY WE PRAY
St. Thérèse, teach us your Little Way of love and trust. Help us seek holiness in the ordinary moments of each day. Pray for us. 🙏

The Café on the Ledger

Upon a ledger swift and plain,
where transfers settle in a breath,
a café opened for the chain—
not vault, not gate, but open hearth.

Its door is marked for all to find:
https://t.co/WaN9PxWSoq, the public hall.
Connect, and leave no key behind;
the signer keeps the assets all.

There wallets speak, and owners keep
the keys that never leave their hand.
No custodian claims the heap;
the signer, only, gives command.

The tokens minted there are small
in cost, yet native to the book:
a fraction of a cent to call
an image into public look.
XLS-20, the standard named,
binds art to ledger, not to myth.
Royalties ride the protocol’s frame;
the trade completes as it is writ.

Collectors come with XRP,
a reserve to wake the account,
and offers set for all to see—
a listing, bid, or brief recount.

The café takes its modest fee
when buyer meets the seller’s price;
the rest returns along the sea
of liquidity, precise.

A creator lays the layers down,
or uploads files already made,
and launches, for a measured sum,
a mint the community may trade.
Allowlists, schedules, trait and rare—
the page goes live; the wallet signs.
Three seconds, and the token’s there,
settled where the Ledger shines.

To trade is not to hoard alone,
nor mint to chase a fleeting name.
Each signature supports the stone
on which the public record came.

So raise a cup, if cup there be,
of code and care and open books:
the café serves the Ledger free
of locked-up keys and shadowed nooks.

Support it thus—create, collect,
confirm, and let the network run.
The ballad ends where use connects
the many to the Ledger’s one.
At https://t.co/WaN9PxWSoq the work is done.

text:
Okay..so you are not a coffee drinker...
Options:

Drinking a refreshing glass of cold water first thing in the morning rehydrates your body and helps jump-start your alertness.
Several other habits, drinks, and natural methods can also help wake you up without relying on coffee.
Alternative Morning Drinks
Green tea and matcha: Contain caffeine paired with L-theanine, an amino acid that provides calm, focused energy without the jittery rush or crash of coffee.
Black tea or masala chai: Provide a robust, caffeinated boost along with warming spices that stimulate the senses.
Yerba mate: Delivers a strong caffeine kick similar to coffee, but with a smoother and more balanced lift.
Chicory coffee: Offers a rich, nutty, and bold flavor like real coffee completely naturally without any caffeine.
Lemon or peppermint herbal tea: Steeps into a bright, refreshing brew that stimulates your palate and wakes up your senses.
Physical and Environmental Habits
• Morning sunlight: Step outside for 10 to 15 minutes to signal your circadian rhythm that the day has begun and reduce grogginess.
• Light exercise: Do a quick stretch, yoga routine, or short walk to increase blood flow to your brain and boost your metabolism.
• Aromatherapy: Inhale invigorating scents like peppermint, eucalyptus, or citrus to instantly jump-start your nervous system.
• Cold water splash: Wash your face with cold water or take a brief cool shower to shock your system into alertness.

WHY BLUE-GREY CHOSE ZYBEK SPORTS: BECAUSE THE NUMBERS HAVE TO MATTER

In today’s recruiting world, athletes are constantly posting 40-yard dash times, shuttle numbers and vertical jumps. But there is an important question college coaches and scouts have to ask: Who verified the numbers?

That is one of the biggest reasons the Blue-Grey All-American Scouting Combine chose Zybek Sports for athletic testing.

Zybek brings the same type of automated timing technology associated with the NFL Scouting Combine to the evaluation process. Instead of relying solely on a handheld stopwatch, electronic testing creates a more consistent standard for athletes competing at the same event.

For Blue-Grey and R2Scouting, that credibility is important. The purpose of the combine isn't simply to produce impressive numbers. It is to give prospects an opportunity to compete, be evaluated and leave with testing results that can strengthen their recruiting profile.

The 40-yard dash is a perfect example. A fraction of a second can make a major difference when evaluating speed. Electronic timing helps reduce the human reaction involved with starting and stopping a stopwatch.

That creates a simple philosophy for the Blue-Grey All-American Scouting Combine:

Your reputation doesn't run the 40. Your offers don't run it. Your social-media following doesn't run it. YOU DO.

text:
I’m afraid the chances of anyone getting a day or two to do what amounts to an investigation with the freedom to talk to anyone and inspect everything and then share you opinions with world are not 5%.  They are 0.0%.  There is no upside for $EOSE .  

In the best case scenario, the investigator says all is well and shares exciting “evidence” that this is the buy of the century.  That’s not much better than what the company already tries to communicate with themselves or what existing bulls (including professional analysts) try to portray.  Maybe there is a tiny upside if it’s a respected enthusiast like yourself.  But how can anyone know that the company will execute in accordance with their alleged potential or if the macro environment or other external factors can derail them?  

So, in the best case, it can’t help much.

However, what if the investigator found what they thought were problems?  What if they come on a bad day and the line breaks down?  What if they talk to the most disgruntled employees? What if they choose to look at things using inappropriately high standards?  What if they think they understand what they see, but don’t?  Or, worst of all, what if they see it actually sucks?

There is so much risk to Eos and very little upside to what you propose.  

We all would like to soothe our nerves with more info about the future.  But we can’t expect those we deal with to offer the fullest transparency just because we want it.  

Also, it could be that Eos plain old does not know how things will play out.  They are on the verge of inflecting.  They should adapt to the ever changing landscape.  Long range plans have a way of not happening.  This company already has a problem with things they say not happening.  Let’s see if they can do what they’ve already said and when they are more mature we should be get trustworthy longer range forecasts.

Finally, energy security is becoming an increasingly important issue between Washington and its European allies as governments respond to uncertainty in global fuel supplies.

So, the key themes to watch in the United States today are the midterm elections, inflation, Federal Reserve policy, Treasury yields, and oil prices.

Stay tuned for more updates on the biggest stories shaping America and the world.

text:
INTELLIGENCE BRIEF // 01 OCT 2026  
UNCLASSIFIED 
SUBJECT: Priority conflicts bearing on U.S. strategic interests — expanded assessment

1. RUSSIA–UKRAINE THEATER  
Situation: Ground operations remain positional. Open-source tracking (ISW) assesses Russian net territorial gains since March 2026 as near zero. For calendar year 2026, Ukrainian forces are assessed to have liberated at least 973 km² and 60 settlements while Russian forces seized roughly 148 km² and 40 settlements (net Russian loss of settlements on the year). Ukrainian counterattacks have cleared or contained Russian infiltration groups in the Lyman direction (Operation Vivaldi focused on defeating reinforcing ATV/motorcycle assaults), Kupyansk sector, and Oleksandrivka area. Limited Ukrainian advances were also recorded north of Sumy City near Korchakivka in late September. Russian claims of seizures (Marine, portions of northern Sumy, flag-raisings presented as control) have been repeatedly contradicted by geolocated footage and Ukrainian unit reporting.

Russian main effort remains pressure on the Fortress Belt (Slovyansk–Kramatorsk–Kostiantynivka approaches) from multiple axes, but without confirmed consolidation of new ground in the final days of September. Supporting efforts along the Oskil, northern Kharkiv border, and southern Zaporizhzhia axes show no material advances.

Strike campaign: Moscow has pivoted to long-range attrition. The 29–30 September combined package—nearly 190 strike drones plus ballistic missiles (Iskander-M/S-400 class) and limited Zircon/Onyx employment—was the largest energy-focused strike since the end of the prior heating season. It damaged the Trypillya Thermal Power Plant in Kyiv Oblast and triggered emergency outages. Ukrainian officials describe the effort as intended to disconnect nuclear plants from the grid and isolate Kyiv ahead of winter 2026–27. Russia is also fielding increased numbers of jet-powered Geran-type drones; Ukraine has reported successful field tests of interceptor drones against them. Ukrainian forces continue intermediate-range strikes on Russian oil refining, logistics nodes in Bryansk and occupied Luhansk/Donetsk, and air-defense sites.

Political-military: Putin’s June 2024 theory of victory (slow ground advance forces capitulation) is assessed as stalled. Kremlin messaging now emphasizes the destructive effect of the strike campaign. U.S. President Trump signed the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act on 18 September. Reports of U.S. pressure for Zelensky to travel to Moscow were denied by both U.S. and Ukrainian officials.

U.S. interest implications: Continued European energy and security burden-sharing demands, risk of further Russian hybrid activity (drone airspace violations into Moldova already recorded, potential asset seizures of European firms inside Russia), and sustainment costs for Ukrainian air defense and deep-strike munitions. Direct NATO–Russia combat remains unlikely but escalation pathways via miscalculation or energy coercion are active.

2. U.S.–ISRAEL–IRAN AND ASSOCIATED FRONTS  
Situation: Joint operations designated Epic Fury (U.S.) and Lion’s Roar (Israel) began 28 February 2026. Strikes killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, removed a substantial portion of senior IRGC and military leadership, and inflicted significant damage on nuclear infrastructure including Natanz. Successor leadership consolidated; the regime did not collapse. Iran retained sufficient ballistic-missile and naval capacity to close or threaten the Strait of Hormuz, strike U.S. bases and Gulf targets, and sustain a multi-week missile campaign against Israel.

A Pakistan-brokered ceasefire in April was followed by a 17 June U.S.–Iran memorandum of understanding outlining a 60-day negotiation window and Hormuz reopening steps. Trump declared the MoU “over” on 8 July after Iranian conditions and shipping attacks; both sides resumed kinetic exchanges. Open-source tallies record at least 555 Iranian missiles and drones launched since 7 July (low single-digit daily rates in late September). Brent crude has traded near $106 amid intermittent Hormuz risk. UK monitoring reported commercial vessels hit in the strait in late September.

Diplomacy: Qatar-mediated indirect talks (Witkoff/Kushner channel with Foreign Minister Araghchi) occurred on UNGA margins. Trump stated there was “a lot of momentum” for a deal while rejecting Iranian proposals that included broader conditions (Lebanon, sanctions sequencing, blockade relief). Iranian messaging has alternated between coexistence offers and threats to expand weaponry and geography of the conflict. Trump’s UNGA address framed the choice as a settlement allowing limited rebuilding versus further action that could “annihilate” the Islamic Republic. Additional indirect talks were expected late September; no durable ceasefire has been confirmed.

Related fronts: Gaza ceasefire (built on the earlier 20-point framework) is partial and fragile. Israeli forces control approximately 60 % of the Strip; Hamas retains policing and coercive presence, including public reprisals, in areas vacated by the IDF. Humanitarian conditions remain severe. Hezbollah is degraded but not disarmed; Israeli operations continue in southern Lebanon. Houthis have consolidated coastal positions affecting Bab al-Mandeb approaches and pushed toward Taiz highlands. Israeli elections are scheduled for 27 October, creating incentive for visible military action on secondary fronts.

U.S. interest implications: This is the only theater with ongoing direct U.S. combat employment. Hormuz disruption transmits immediately into global energy prices and Gulf partner security demands. Failure to reach a nuclear and missile constraint agreement leaves residual breakout risk and proxy reactivation pathways. Israeli election dynamics and Gaza governance vacuum add friction to any U.S. diplomatic end-state.

3. PRC COERCION OF TAIWAN  
Situation: No large-scale encirclement or joint-fire exercise is currently underway. Activity has shifted to persistent gray-zone presence. Taiwan Ministry of National Defense daily reporting shows continuous PLA aircraft, naval, and “official” (coast guard/maritime militia) vessel operations. Representative snapshots: 15 aircraft, 8 naval vessels, and 2 official ships (15–16 September), with 12 aircraft crossing the median line; 28 aircraft (17–18 September), 24 crossing; 23 aircraft, 7 naval, and 7 official ships in the 24 hours ending early 1 October, 16 of them crossing into northern, central, and southwestern ADIZ sectors. These are treated as routine rather than crisis indicators.

Political signaling: At the 30 September National Day reception marking the 77th anniversary of the PRC, Xi Jinping used hardened language relative to 2025, calling for efforts to “resolutely strike” Taiwan-independence separatist forces, oppose external interference, and advance reunification. This followed the recent Washington summit in which Xi urged the U.S. side to “oppose” Taiwan independence—stronger formulation than the longstanding U.S. position of not supporting independence. Taiwan is budgeting approximately $850 million for additional munitions and emphasizing local production to extend stocks under blockade conditions. U.S. Navy establishment of a drone command element is noted in open sources as relevant to Taiwan contingency planning.

U.S. interest implications: The operational pattern erodes the median-line norm and raises the baseline for what constitutes normal PLA activity, compressing decision time in any future incident. Economic exposure (semiconductors, sea lines) and alliance credibility (Japan, Philippines, Australia) are directly engaged. Large-scale amphibious assault remains a high-cost, lower-probability contingency; ambiguous incidents inside an already militarized environment are the more proximate risk.

Cross-theater notes: Resource competition is real—air-defense interceptors, long-range strike munitions, naval presence, and diplomatic bandwidth are finite. Russia and Iran retain mutual support channels; China continues economic and dual-use flows that blunt sanctions. No theater shows a near-term decisive military outcome favoring U.S. preferences without sustained external resourcing or a negotiated compromise that cedes core adversary demands.

text:
Limited progress reported in Qatar-mediated US-Iran talks
NEW YORK: Qatar-mediated indirect talks between the United States and Iran have made limited progress, but both sides remain committed to their core demands and continue to disagree on key issues.
People familiar with the negotiations said the deadlock had increased fears that the conflict could once again escalate into large-scale military action. US officials reportedly believe President Donald Trump could order a resumption of military operations against Iran after the November midterm elections.
Qatari mediator Ali al-Thawadi held several hours of talks in New York with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his delegation. The discussions included a two-page Qatari compromise proposal aimed at bridging Iran’s demand for an end to the US naval blockade and Washington’s call for concessions on Tehran’s nuclear programme.
Al-Thawadi later travelled to Washington, where he met US officials and Trump’s envoy Jared Kushner. However, sources said the talks produced no significant breakthrough, with both sides viewing the other’s demands as unacceptable.
Iranian officials have indicated that Tehran would consider concessions on nuclear issues only if Washington agreed to return to the terms of a memorandum of understanding reached in June. President Trump, meanwhile, has denied reports that he offered Iran sanctions relief or other concessions.
Regional mediators, including Pakistan and Egypt, are also urging the sides to compromise. Qatar, however, is reportedly becoming increasingly frustrated with the positions of both Washington and Tehran.

text:
Cove Capital to expand beyond Kazakhstan

Cove Capital, a US-based mining investment firm, is reported to be looking beyond Kazakhstan for opportunities in critical minerals.

The firm has direct ties to the Trump family through its portfolio company Cove Kaz Capital Group, which merged with Skyline Builders in May 2026. Donald Trump Jr and Eric Trump both hold strategic investments in Skyline. Cove Kaz Capital is developing a major tungsten project in Kazakhstan together with the state-owned mining firm JSC Tau-Ken Samruk, operating as Kaz Resources.

Kaz Resources is now developing the world’s largest known undeveloped tungsten resource in Kazakhstan.

Controversially, the tungsten project was offered up to US$1.6 billion ($2.3 billion) in US Government financing in a deal announced at the C5+1 Leaders Summit in Washington, DC, on 6 November 2025. Donald Trump’s sons are set to gain an interest in Kaz Resources through their investment in Skyline. However, they have stated that they are passive shareholders, having had no prior knowledge of the commitment to the project.

The projects in which Cove Kaz holds a 70% stake contain about 1.4 million tonnes (Mt) of tungsten trioxide. This accounts for about 70% of Kazakhstan’s total resources. China currently controls about 80% of global concentrate production of tungsten and holds around 2.4Mt of reserves.

Cove Kaz plans to start tungsten production in 2030, ramping up to about 5,000 tonnes per year in its first phase before rising to 12,000 tonnes at full build-out. The firm is ramping up toward a Feasibility Study to be completed before the end of 2027, though site preparation work will likely begin before then.

Cove Capital is looking across Central Asia for opportunities in Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, as well as the Caucasus, eyeing copper and other critical mineral assets. This aligns with the US Government’s efforts to secure supplies of critical minerals needed for defence, the energy transition, advanced technologies, and energy security.

Reuters reports that Cove Capital CEO Pini Althaus says the firm is actively involved in a number of discussions regarding tier-one asset opportunities.
